<div class="domain-heading">Demographics</div>
<p class="domain-description">Demographics contains subject identity, enrollment, study participation, longitudinal episode structure, survival status, family and medical history, and other contextual information needed to interpret records across the model.</p>

<section id="class-externalreference" class="class-section" data-subsets="base aml ls nbl" markdown="1">

<section id="class-familymedicalhistory" class="class-section" data-subsets="base fa hl ls rb" markdown="1">

<section id="class-medicalhistory" class="class-section" data-subsets="base all aml ews gct hl ls lt nrsts os pre rb" markdown="1">

## MedicalHistory <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">MedicalHistory records prior or concurrent conditions and selected background health factors for the subject, supporting interpretation of diagnosis, risk, treatment, and outcomes.</p>

<div class="domain-banner domain-testing">
<div class="domain-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-dna-icon lucide-dna"><path d="m10 16 1.5 1.5"/><path d="m14 8-1.5-1.5"/><path d="M15 2c-1.798 1.998-2.518 3.995-2.807 5.993"/><path d="m16.5 10.5 1 1"/><path d="m17 6-2.891-2.891"/><path d="M2 15c6.667-6 13.333 0 20-6"/><path d="m20 9 .891.891"/><path d="M3.109 14.109 4 15"/><path d="m6.5 12.5 1 1"/><path d="m7 18 2.891 2.891"/><path d="M9 22c1.798-1.998 2.518-3.995 2.807-5.993"/></svg></div>
<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Testing</div>
<p class="domain-description">Testing contains laboratory, pathology, genomic, functional, anthropometric, and specimen-related observations used to characterize subjects, disease biology, eligibility, monitoring, and research sample availability.</p>
</div>
</div>

<section id="class-vitalsandanthropometrics" class="class-section" data-subsets="base all aml cns ews fa fprh gct hl ls os pre" markdown="1">

## VitalsAndAnthropometrics <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">VitalsAndAnthropometrics records physical measurements such as anthropometrics, vital measurements, measurement units, values, and gestational age at birth where relevant.</p>

<section id="class-geneticanalysis" class="class-section" data-subsets="base all aml cns ews fa gct ls nbl nrsts pre rb rms" markdown="1">

## GeneticAnalysis <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">GeneticAnalysis captures germline and somatic genomic findings, testing context, specimens, methods, genes, variants, copy number, cytogenetic findings, HGVS expressions, significance, inheritance, and related genomic interpretation fields.</p>

<section id="class-biospecimen" class="class-section" data-subsets="base aml gct hl ls nbl nrsts rms" markdown="1">

## Biospecimen <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">Biospecimen describes collected or stored biospecimens, including specimen type, container, media, and available quantity, supporting specimen tracking and downstream research use.</p>

<div class="domain-banner domain-disease-attributes">
<div class="domain-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-network-icon lucide-network"><rect x="16" y="16" width="6" height="6" rx="1"/><rect x="2" y="16" width="6" height="6" rx="1"/><rect x="9" y="2" width="6" height="6" rx="1"/><path d="M5 16v-3a1 1 0 0 1 1-1h12a1 1 0 0 1 1 1v3"/><path d="M12 12V8"/></svg></div>
<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Disease Attributes</div>
<p class="domain-description">Disease Attributes contains diagnostic, staging, anatomic, histologic, biologic, risk, extent-of-disease, and disease-site concepts used to characterize the subject's cancer or cancer-related condition.</p>
</div>
</div>

<section id="class-diagnosis" class="class-section" data-subsets="base all aml cns ews fa fprh gct hl ls lt nbl npc nrsts os pre rb rms" markdown="1">

## Diagnosis <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>1..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">Diagnosis captures disease diagnosis and diagnostic assessment details, including timing, review source, diagnosis basis, diagnosis category, morphology, histology, disease-specific diagnostic flags, and transformation information.</p>

<section id="class-diseasecharacteristics" class="class-section" data-subsets="base all ews fa fprh gct hl ls nbl rb" markdown="1">

## DiseaseCharacteristics <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">DiseaseCharacteristics captures additional disease-level attributes such as risk group, imaging response scores, performance status, clinical findings, presentation symptoms, and disease-specific biologic or clinical characteristics.</p>

<div class="domain-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-hospital-icon lucide-hospital"><path d="M12 7v4"/><path d="M14 21v-3a2 2 0 0 0-4 0v3"/><path d="M14 9h-4"/><path d="M18 11h2a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H4a2 2 0 0 1-2-2v-9a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h2"/><path d="M18 21V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H8a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v16"/></svg></div>
<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Intervention</div>
<p class="domain-description">Intervention contains treatment and procedure records, including surgery, medications, radiation therapy, transplantation, transfusion, cellular therapy, locoregional therapy, fertility preservation procedures, and protocol treatment modifications.</p>
</div>
</div>

<section id="class-surgicalprocedures" class="class-section" data-subsets="base cns ews fa fprh gct hl ls lt npc nrsts os pre rb rms" markdown="1">

## SurgicalProcedures <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">SurgicalProcedures records biopsy, resection, procedural, and surgery-related interventions, including site, laterality, extent, margins, complications, outcome, and disease-specific surgical details.</p>

<section id="class-medication" class="class-section" data-subsets="base cns ews fa fprh gct hl ls lt npc os rb" markdown="1">

## Medication <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">Medication captures medication exposure and administration details, including chemotherapy or supportive care agents, regimen, route, dose, frequency, cumulative exposure, timing, and protocol or non-protocol context.</p>

<section id="class-stemcelltransplant" class="class-section" data-subsets="base all aml ews fa fprh gct hl rb" markdown="1">

## StemCellTransplant <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">StemCellTransplant records hematopoietic stem cell transplant details, including timing, transplant type, donor relationship, HLA matching, conditioning, cell source, CD34 collection or infusion, chimerism, and recovery status.</p>

<section id="class-fertilityprocedures" class="class-section" data-subsets="base fprh" markdown="1">

## FertilityProcedures <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<section id="domain-monitoring" class="domain-section" data-domain="monitoring" markdown="1">

<div class="domain-banner domain-monitoring">
<div class="domain-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-stethoscope-icon lucide-stethoscope"><path d="M11 2v2"/><path d="M5 2v2"/><path d="M5 3H4a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v4a6 6 0 0 0 12 0V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2h-1"/><path d="M8 15a6 6 0 0 0 12 0v-3"/><circle cx="20" cy="10" r="2"/></svg></div>
<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Monitoring</div>
<p class="domain-description">Monitoring contains response, residual disease, toxicity, late effects, subsequent neoplasms, reproductive outcomes, patient-reported outcomes, and other follow-up concepts used to evaluate disease course and treatment impact over time.</p>
</div>
</div>

<section id="class-subjectresponse" class="class-section" data-subsets="base aml cns ews gct hl ls lt nbl npc nrsts os rb rms" markdown="1">

## SubjectResponse <a class="class-cardinality" href="/documentation/#cardinality-required-fields-and-tiering" title="Learn about class cardinality"><code>0..*</code></a>

<p class="class-description">SubjectResponse captures response assessments across disease sites and treatment time points, including response methods, categories, systems, scores, marrow findings, imaging findings, necrosis, symptoms, and disease-specific response details.</p>

Natural menopause usually occurs around age 50. A woman is said to be in menopause when she hasn't had a period for 12 months in a row. Symptoms of menopause include hot flashes, mood swings, night sweats, vaginal dryness, trouble concentrating, and infertility. Premature menopause can be caused by some cancer treatments, surgery to remove the ovaries, and certain diseases or genetic conditions."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition in which the ovaries stop working and menstrual periods stop before age 40. Natural menopause usually occurs around age 50. A woman is said to be in menopause when she hasn't had a period for 12 months in a row. Symptoms of menopause include hot flashes, mood swings, night sweats, vaginal dryness, trouble concentrating, and infertility. Premature menopause can be caused by some cancer treatments, surgery to remove the ovaries, and certain diseases or genetic conditions.</span></summary></details></td><td class="slot-range" title="YesNoEnum"><span><button type="button" class="enum-link" onclick="openEnumModal('enum-modal-yesnoenum')">YesNoEnum</button></span></td></tr></tbody></table><div class="slot-icon-legend"><span class="text-delta slot-icon-legend-label">Slot Icons:</span><span class="slot-icon-legend-item"><span class="slot-icon-legend-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="10" height="10" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="#6b7280" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-asterisk-icon lucide-asterisk"><path d="M12 6v12"/><path d="M17.196 9 6.804 15"/><path d="m6.804 9 10.392 6"/></svg></span>Required</span><span class="slot-icon-legend-item priority-legend-item" style="display:none;">;<span class="slot-icon-legend-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="#6b7280" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-dot-icon lucide-dot"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1"/></svg></span>Priority</span></div></div>

Symptoms include blurred, cloudy, or double vision; sensitivity to light; and difficulty seeing at night. Without treatment, cataracts can cause blindness. There are many different types and causes of cataracts. They may occur in people of all ages, but are most common in the elderly.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C26713"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C26713" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C26713</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base all cns rb pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="5' UTR"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="5' UTR" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C13371" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>5' UTR</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="Sequences on the 5' end of messenger RNAs that are not translated into protein.  5'UTR extends from the transcription start site to just before the ATG translation initiation codon. This region contains the ribosome binding site and other transcription and translation regulating sequences.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C13371"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C13371" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C13371</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base all cns ls rb"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Intronic"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Intronic" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C45387" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Intronic</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="Single Nucleotide Polymorphism in Intronic Sequences (Intronic SNP) consists of a variation at an appreciable frequency between individuals of a single interbreeding population of a single nucleotide, due to base substitution, at an equivalent location within a transcribed non-coding intervening DNA sequence separating protein-coding sequences (exons) in an eukaryotic nuclear gene. Poorly conserved and of variable length and number, intron sequences are removed from nascent message RNA transcripts in the nucleus after the 5' cap and polyA tail have been added. Self-complementary sequences at exon-intron junctions form a hairpin structure recognized by enzymes that splice exons together into a mature mRNA that is ready for translation in the cytoplasm. When the intron is removed, the donor junction at the 5' end of the intron is spliced to the acceptor junction at the 3' end of the intron."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Single Nucleotide Polymorphism in Intronic Sequences (Intronic SNP) consists of a variation at an appreciable frequency between individuals of a single interbreeding population of a single nucleotide, due to base substitution, at an equivalent location within a transcribed non-coding intervening DNA sequence separating protein-coding sequences (exons) in an eukaryotic nuclear gene. Poorly conserved and of variable length and number, intron sequences are removed from nascent message RNA transcripts in the nucleus after the 5' cap and polyA tail have been added. Self-complementary sequences at exon-intron junctions form a hairpin structure recognized by enzymes that splice exons together into a mature mRNA that is ready for translation in the cytoplasm. When the intron is removed, the donor junction at the 5' end of the intron is spliced to the acceptor junction at the 3' end of the intron.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C45387"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C45387" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C45387</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base all cns ls"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Splice Site"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Splice Site" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C45574" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Splice Site</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited single base substitution in a sequence of eukaryotic DNA located in either an acceptor (3' or downstream) or donor (5' or upstream) splice site of a gene. Functional single nucleotide polymorphisms in these intron-exon junctions can cause incorrect RNA splicing which, in turn, alters gene expression."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An inherited single base substitution in a sequence of eukaryotic DNA located in either an acceptor (3' or downstream) or donor (5' or upstream) splice site of a gene. Clinical presentation occurs in the middle decades and is characterized by the proximal development of multiple (but less than 100), non-polypoid colonic adenomas. Clinical progression to colorectal cancer may occur later in life but the risk is less than with classic FAP.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6729"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C6729" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C6729</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="BAP1 Tumor Predisposition Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="BAP1 Tumor Predisposition Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C172639" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>BAP1 Tumor Predisposition Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant inherited tumor predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in the BAP1 gene. <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome/Isolated Hemihyperplasia"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome/Isolated Hemihyperplasia" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34415" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome/Isolated Hemihyperplasia</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A complex syndrome resulting from various genetic and epigenetic anomalies of the 11p15.5 chromosomal region, leading to dysregulated expression of imprinted genes. Specific genes involved include CDKN1C, H19, IGF2, and KCNQ1OT1. One of the key genetic anomalies is an imbalance between the paternally expressed IGF2 growth enhancer gene and the maternally expressed H19 growth suppressor gene, leading to fetal and postnatal overgrowth. The condition is typically characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, umbilical hernia or more severe abdominal wall anomalies such as omphalocele, ear lobe indentations, and hypoglycemia associated with hyperinsulinemia due to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia. Patients with this syndrome have an increased risk for development of embryonal tumors (particularly Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma) and adrenal cortex carcinoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A complex syndrome resulting from various genetic and epigenetic anomalies of the 11p15.5 chromosomal region, leading to dysregulated expression of imprinted genes. Specific genes involved include CDKN1C, H19, IGF2, and KCNQ1OT1. One of the key genetic anomalies is an imbalance between the paternally expressed IGF2 growth enhancer gene and the maternally expressed H19 growth suppressor gene, leading to fetal and postnatal overgrowth. The condition is typically characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, umbilical hernia or more severe abdominal wall anomalies such as omphalocele, ear lobe indentations, and hypoglycemia associated with hyperinsulinemia due to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia. Patients with this syndrome have an increased risk for development of embryonal tumors (particularly Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma) and adrenal cortex carcinoma.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34415"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C34415" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C34415</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C28244" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare genetic syndrome with an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance. It is caused by a mutation in the FLCN gene which encodes the protein folliculin. Clinical signs include multiple benign growths of the skin and lungs that begin to manifest in the second or third decade of life. The clinical course is characterized by the progressive growth of new and existing neoplasms. In those with mutations in both copies of FLCN, the kidneys may also be affected by the growth of benign or malignant neoplasms."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare genetic syndrome with an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance. It is caused by a mutation in the FLCN gene which encodes the protein folliculin. Clinical signs include multiple benign growths of the skin and lungs that begin to manifest in the second or third decade of life. The clinical course is characterized by the progressive growth of new and existing neoplasms. In those with mutations in both copies of FLCN, the kidneys may also be affected by the growth of benign or malignant neoplasms.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C28244"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C28244" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C28244</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bloom Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bloom Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2903" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bloom Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare, inherited disorder marked by height that is shorter than average, a narrow face with redness and a rash, a high-pitched voice, and fertility problems. Patients with this disorder have an increased risk of cancer, especially leukemia and osteosarcoma (bone cancer). Bloom syndrome is caused by changes in a protein that normally helps cells make copies of the DNA. Changes in this protein cause many breaks, rearrangements, and other mutations in the DNA. It is a type of autosomal recessive genetic disease."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, inherited disorder marked by height that is shorter than average, a narrow face with redness and a rash, a high-pitched voice, and fertility problems. Patients with this disorder have an increased risk of cancer, especially leukemia and osteosarcoma (bone cancer). Bloom syndrome is caused by changes in a protein that normally helps cells make copies of the DNA. Changes in this protein cause many breaks, rearrangements, and other mutations in the DNA. It is a type of autosomal recessive genetic disease.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2903"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C2903" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C2903</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="CBL Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="CBL Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C176942" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>CBL Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the CBL gene, encoding E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase CBL. Affected individuals may have an increased risk for certain malignancies, particularly juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the CBL gene, encoding E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase CBL. The condition resembles Noonan syndrome 1 and is characterized by facial dysmorphism, a wide spectrum of cardiac disease, reduced growth, variable cognitive deficits, and ectodermal and musculoskeletal anomalies. Affected individuals may have an increased risk for certain malignancies, particularly juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C176942"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C176942" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C176942</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="DICER1 Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="DICER1 Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C123317" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>DICER1 Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant inherited tumor predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations of the DICER1 gene. Carriers are at an increased risk of developing benign and malignant neoplasms, including pleuropulmonary blastoma, childhood cystic nephroma, goiter, thyroid carcinoma, pineoblastoma, DICER1-mutant ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, and primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C123317"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C123317" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C123317</a></span></td></tr>

In about half the cases mutations in the TERT, TERC, DKC1, or TINF2 genes are identified.  Patients are at an increased risk of developing bone marrow failure, myelodysplastic syndrome, leukemia, or cancer, especially in the head and neck region."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare genetic disorder characterized by nail dystrophy, reticulated skin pigmentation especially on the neck and chest, and oral leukoplakia.  In about half the cases mutations in the TERT, TERC, DKC1, or TINF2 genes are identified.  Patients are at an increased risk of developing bone marrow failure, myelodysplastic syndrome, leukemia, or cancer, especially in the head and neck region.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C111802"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C111802" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C111802</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="ETV6-Related Thrombocytopenia and Leukemia Predisposition"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="ETV6-Related Thrombocytopenia and Leukemia Predisposition" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C178386" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>ETV6-Related Thrombocytopenia and Leukemia Predisposition</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant condition caused by mutation(s) in the ETV6 gene, encoding transcription factor ETV6. It is characterized by an increased risk of developing thrombocytopenia and diverse hematologic malignancies, including myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, B lymphoblastic leukemia, and plasma cell myeloma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant condition caused by mutation(s) in the ETV6 gene, encoding transcription factor ETV6. It is characterized by an increased risk of developing thrombocytopenia and diverse hematologic malignancies, including myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, B lymphoblastic leukemia, and plasma cell myeloma.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C178386"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C178386" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C178386</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Familial Adenomatous Polyposis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Familial Adenomatous Polyposis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3339" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Familial Adenomatous Polyposis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant disorder, characterized by the presence of multiple adenomas in the colon and rectum. It is caused by a germline mutation in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene which is located on the long arm of chromosome 5. The adenomas are most often tubular, and they have the tendency to progress to adenocarcinoma. They can occur throughout the colon, but they tend to concentrate in the rectum and sigmoid colon. The colorectal adenomas are detected during endoscopic examination between the age of 10 and 20 years. The adenomas increase in size and numbers with age, and there is usually progression of one or more adenomas to adenocarcinoma. The mean age of development of adenocarcinoma is about 40 years. Signs include rectal bleeding and mucousy diarrhea."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant disorder, characterized by the presence of multiple adenomas in the colon and rectum. It is caused by a germline mutation in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene which is located on the long arm of chromosome 5. The adenomas are most often tubular, and they have the tendency to progress to adenocarcinoma. They can occur throughout the colon, but they tend to concentrate in the rectum and sigmoid colon. The colorectal adenomas are detected during endoscopic examination between the age of 10 and 20 years. The adenomas increase in size and numbers with age, and there is usually progression of one or more adenomas to adenocarcinoma. The mean age of development of adenocarcinoma is about 40 years. Signs include rectal bleeding and mucousy diarrhea.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3339"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3339" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3339</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Familial Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Familial Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C176906" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Familial Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the KIT or PDGFRA genes, encoding mast/stem cell growth factor receptor Kit and platelet derived growth factor receptor alpha respectively. The condition is characterized by the occurrence of multiple gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the KIT or PDGFRA genes, encoding mast/stem cell growth factor receptor Kit and platelet derived growth factor receptor alpha respectively. <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Familial Platelet Disorder and AML Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Familial Platelet Disorder and AML Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C41527" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Familial Platelet Disorder and AML Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="Androgen Activity Induction involves initiation of the biological function of biochemical substances (androgens) secreted by the testes that have a specific regulatory effect on the activity of cells involved in development and maintenance of male sex characteristics."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Androgen Activity Induction involves initiation of the biological function of biochemical substances (androgens) secreted by the testes that have a specific regulatory effect on the activity of cells involved in development and maintenance of male sex characteristics.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C41527"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C41527" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C41527</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Fanconi Anemia"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Fanconi Anemia" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C62505" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Fanconi Anemia</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chromosomal instability syndrome that is the most common form of inherited aplastic anemia. In addition to bone marrow failure, it is associated with skeletal abnormalities and increased incidence of the development of malignancy. Multiple genes are responsible for Fanconi anemia."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chromosomal instability syndrome that is the most common form of inherited aplastic anemia. It is inherited as an autosomal recessive or X-linked disorder. In addition to bone marrow failure, it is associated with skeletal abnormalities and increased incidence of the development of malignancy. <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="LEOPARD Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="LEOPARD Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84820" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>LEOPARD Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A genetic syndrome caused by mutation(s) in the PTPN11, RAF1, or the BRAF genes, encoding tyrosine-protein phosphatase non-receptor type 11 and RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase, and serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf, respectively. Affected male individuals may exhibit unilateral or bilateral cryptorchidism, small penis, and/or hypospadias (urinary meatus on the dorsal side of the penis). Affected female individuals may have ovarian hypoplasia or agenesis. Primary hypogonadism in both female and male individuals may result in delayed puberty."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A genetic syndrome caused by mutation(s) in the PTPN11, RAF1, or the BRAF genes, encoding tyrosine-protein phosphatase non-receptor type 11 and RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase, and serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf, respectively. Affected male individuals may exhibit unilateral or bilateral cryptorchidism, small penis, and/or hypospadias (urinary meatus on the dorsal side of the penis). Affected female individuals may have ovarian hypoplasia or agenesis. Primary hypogonadism in both female and male individuals may result in delayed puberty.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84820"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C84820" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C84820</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Legius Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Legius Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C176941" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Legius Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the SPRED1 gene, encoding sprouty-related, EVH1 domain-containing protein 1. The condition resembles neurofibromatosis type I but is less severe. The condition resembles neurofibromatosis type I but is less severe. <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Lynch Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Lynch Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C8494" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Lynch Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant hereditary neoplastic syndrome characterized by the development of colorectal carcinoma and a high risk of developing endometrial carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, and small intestinal carcinoma. Patients often develop colorectal carcinomas at an early age (mean, 45 years). In the majority of the cases the lesions arise from the proximal colon. At the molecular level, high-frequency microsatellite instability is present."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant hereditary neoplastic syndrome characterized by the development of colorectal carcinoma and a high risk of developing endometrial carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, and small intestinal carcinoma. Patients often develop colorectal carcinomas at an early age (mean, 45 years). In the majority of the cases the lesions arise from the proximal colon. At the molecular level, high-frequency microsatellite instability is present.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C8494"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C8494" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C8494</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="MUTYH-Associated Polyposis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="MUTYH-Associated Polyposis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C96520" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>MUTYH-Associated Polyposis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal recessive hereditary neoplastic syndrome caused by mutations in the MUTYH gene on chromosome 1p34.1. This condition is associated with characteristic facial features, including hypertelorism, pubertal delay, occasional progressive cardiomyopathy, insulin resistance with type 2 diabetes, and an increased risk for Wilms tumor."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutation(s) in the TRIM37 gene, encoding E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase TRIM37. <tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Kidney Failure"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Kidney Failure" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C4376" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Kidney Failure</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A condition in which the kidneys stop working and are not able to remove waste and extra water from the blood or keep body chemicals in balance. Acute or severe renal failure happens suddenly (for example, after an injury) and may be treated and cured. Chronic renal failure develops over many years, may be caused by conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes, and cannot be cured. Chronic renal failure may lead to total and long-lasting renal failure, called end-stage renal disease (ESRD). A person in ESRD needs dialysis (the process of cleaning the blood by passing it through a membrane or filter) or a kidney transplant."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition in which the kidneys stop working and are not able to remove waste and extra water from the blood or keep body chemicals in balance. Acute or severe renal failure happens suddenly (for example, after an injury) and may be treated and cured. Chronic renal failure develops over many years, may be caused by conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes, and cannot be cured. Chronic renal failure may lead to total and long-lasting renal failure, called end-stage renal disease (ESRD). A person in ESRD needs dialysis (the process of cleaning the blood by passing it through a membrane or filter) or a kidney transplant.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C4376"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C4376" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C4376</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Liver Failure"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Liver Failure" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C26922" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Liver Failure</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A disorder characterized by the inability of the liver to metabolize chemicals in the body. Causes include cirrhosis and drug-induced hepatotoxicity. Signs and symptoms include jaundice and encephalopathy. Laboratory test results reveal abnormal plasma levels of ammonia, bilirubin, lactic dehydrogenase, and alkaline phosphatase."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A disorder characterized by the inability of the liver to metabolize chemicals in the body. Causes include cirrhosis and drug-induced hepatotoxicity. Signs and symptoms include jaundice and encephalopathy. Laboratory test results reveal abnormal plasma levels of ammonia, bilirubin, lactic dehydrogenase, and alkaline phosphatase.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C26922"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C26922" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C26922</a></span></td></tr>

It results in the presence of a single vessel instead of two vessels leading out of the heart. Clinical signs and symptoms include cyanosis that is present at birth, poor growth, dyspnea, tachypnea, arrhythmia, cardiomegaly, and heart failure. If it is not surgically repaired, it leads to death."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare congenital cardiovascular disorder characterized by the failure of the embryologic structure truncus arteriosus to divide into the aorta and pulmonary trunk. It results in the presence of a single vessel instead of two vessels leading out of the heart. Clinical signs and symptoms include cyanosis that is present at birth, poor growth, dyspnea, tachypnea, arrhythmia, cardiomegaly, and heart failure. The primary objective of the organization is to conduct clinical trials of new therapies for childhood and adolescent cancer. COG develops and coordinates clinical trials conducted at the 238 member institutions that include cancer centers of all major universities and teaching hospitals throughout the U.S. and Canada, as well as sites in Europe and Australia. COG members include over 5000 cancer researchers."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An NCI-supported clinical cooperative group formed by the merger of the four national pediatric cancer research organizations: the Children's Cancer Group, the Intergroup Rhabdomyosarcoma Study Group, the National Wilms Tumor Study Group, and the Pediatric Oncology Group. The primary objective of the organization is to conduct clinical trials of new therapies for childhood and adolescent cancer. COG develops and coordinates clinical trials conducted at the 238 member institutions that include cancer centers of all major universities and teaching hospitals throughout the U.S. and Canada, as well as sites in Europe and Australia. COG members include over 5000 cancer researchers.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C39353"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C39353" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C39353</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="SIOP MMT"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="SIOP MMT" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C192775" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>SIOP MMT</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An international pediatric oncology committee that specializes in the research of malignant mesenchymal tumors. Along with the Associazione Italiana Ematologia Oncologia Pediatrica-Soft Tissue Sarcoma Committee (AIEOP-STSC), which was formerly known as the Italian Cooperative Group (ICG), SIOP-MMT founded the European pediatric Soft tissue sarcoma Study Group (EpSSG) and the Non-rhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma (NRSTS) study in 2005 with the goal of making pediatric non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcoma treatment uniform across Europe."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An international pediatric oncology committee that specializes in the research of malignant mesenchymal tumors. Along with the Associazione Italiana Ematologia Oncologia Pediatrica-Soft Tissue Sarcoma Committee (AIEOP-STSC), which was formerly known as the Italian Cooperative Group (ICG), SIOP-MMT founded the European pediatric Soft tissue sarcoma Study Group (EpSSG) and the Non-rhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma (NRSTS) study in 2005 with the goal of making pediatric non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcoma treatment uniform across Europe.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C192775"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C192775" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C192775</a></span></td></tr>

Gallium binds to transferrin, leukocyte lactoferrin, bacterial siderophores and inflammatory proteins and thereby can be used to localize foci of infection. A lumpectomy to remove a breast tumor is a type of open biopsy."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A procedure in which a surgical incision (cut) is made through the skin to expose and remove tissues. The biopsy tissue is examined under a microscope by a pathologist. An open biopsy may be done in the doctor's office or in the hospital, and may use local anesthesia or general anesthesia. A lumpectomy to remove a breast tumor is a type of open biopsy.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C15386"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C15386" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C15386</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns ews fa hl ls npc pre rb"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="MRI"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="MRI" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C16809" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>MRI</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A procedure in which radio waves and a powerful magnet linked to a computer are used to create detailed pictures of areas inside the body. NMRI makes better images of organs and soft tissue than other scanning techniques, such as computed tomography (CT) or x-ray. NMRI is especially useful for imaging the brain, the spine, the soft tissue of joints, and the inside of bones."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A procedure in which radio waves and a powerful magnet linked to a computer are used to create detailed pictures of areas inside the body. These pictures can show the difference between normal and diseased tissue. NMRI makes better images of organs and soft tissue than other scanning techniques, such as computed tomography (CT) or x-ray. <tr data-subsets="base fa gct hl ls npc pre rb"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="PET Scan"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="PET Scan" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C17007" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>PET Scan</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A procedure in which a small amount of radioactive glucose (sugar) is injected into a vein, and a scanner is used to make detailed, computerized pictures of areas inside the body where the glucose is used. <tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Alveolar Soft-Part Sarcoma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Alveolar Soft-Part Sarcoma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3750" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Alveolar Soft-Part Sarcoma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of large epithelioid cells with abundant cytoplasm forming nests and pseudoalveolar structures. The groups of the epithelioid cells are separated by thin-walled sinusoidal spaces. It occurs most often in adolescents and young adults. In adults the most common sites of involvement are the extremities, and in infants and children, the head and neck. It usually presents as a slowly growing mass and it frequently metastasizes to other anatomic sites. The most common sites of metastasis are the lungs, bone, and brain."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of large epithelioid cells with abundant cytoplasm forming nests and pseudoalveolar structures. The groups of the epithelioid cells are separated by thin-walled sinusoidal spaces. It occurs most often in adolescents and young adults. In adults the most common sites of involvement are the extremities, and in infants and children, the head and neck. It usually presents as a slowly growing mass and it frequently metastasizes to other anatomic sites. The most common sites of metastasis are the lungs, bone, and brain.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3750"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3750" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3750</a></span></td></tr>

However, the correlation of histological anaplasia with clinical outcome is inconsistent. (Adapted from WHO)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A WHO grade III neuroepithelial neoplasm composed of neoplastic, mature ganglion cells and anaplastic glial cells. The anaplastic changes in the glial component and high MIB-1 and TP53 labeling indices may indicate aggressive behavior. However, the correlation of histological anaplasia with clinical outcome is inconsistent. <tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3720" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A peripheral (mature) T-cell lymphoma, consisting of usually large anaplastic, CD30 positive cells. The majority of cases are positive for the anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK) protein. The most frequently seen genetic alteration is a t(2;5) translocation. Majority of patients present with advanced disease. The most important prognostic indicator is ALK positivity, which has been associated with a favorable prognosis. (WHO, 2001)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A peripheral (mature) T-cell lymphoma, consisting of usually large anaplastic, CD30 positive cells. The majority of cases are positive for the anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK) protein. The most frequently seen genetic alteration is a t(2;5) translocation. Majority of patients present with advanced disease. The most important prognostic indicator is ALK positivity, which has been associated with a favorable prognosis. (WHO, 2001)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3720"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3720" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3720</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Atypical Fibroxanthoma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Atypical Fibroxanthoma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C4246" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Atypical Fibroxanthoma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An intermediate cutaneous mesenchymal neoplasm of uncertain differentiation, usually affecting the actinic-damaged skin of the elderly.  The tumor presents as a single cutaneous nodule which is often ulcerated.  Microscopically, it is characterized by the presence of highly atypical cytologic features, pleomorphism and abundant mitotic figures. The vast majority of patients have an excellent prognosis following conservative therapy. Recurrences are infrequent, and metastasis is rare."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An intermediate cutaneous mesenchymal neoplasm of uncertain differentiation, usually affecting the actinic-damaged skin of the elderly.  The tumor presents as a single cutaneous nodule which is often ulcerated.  Microscopically, it is characterized by the presence of highly atypical cytologic features, pleomorphism and abundant mitotic figures. The vast majority of patients have an excellent prognosis following conservative therapy. Recurrences are infrequent, and metastasis is rare.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C4246"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C4246" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C4246</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Atypical Lipomatous Tumor"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Atypical Lipomatous Tumor" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6505" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Atypical Lipomatous Tumor</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A locally aggressive mesenchymal neoplasm composed either entirely or partly of an adipocytic proliferation showing at least focal nuclear atypia in both adipocytes and stromal cells. &quot;Atypical lipomatous tumor&quot; and &quot;well-differentiated liposarcoma&quot; are synonyms describing lesions that are morphologically and genetically identical. Amplification of MDM2 and/or CDK4 is almost always present. (WHO 2020)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A locally aggressive mesenchymal neoplasm composed either entirely or partly of an adipocytic proliferation showing at least focal nuclear atypia in both adipocytes and stromal cells. "Atypical lipomatous tumor" and "well-differentiated liposarcoma" are synonyms describing lesions that are morphologically and genetically identical. Amplification of MDM2 and/or CDK4 is almost always present. (WHO 2020)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6505"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C6505" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C6505</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Atypical Teratoid/Rhabdoid Tumor, NOS or NEC"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Atypical Teratoid/Rhabdoid Tumor, NOS or NEC" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6906" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Atypical Teratoid/Rhabdoid Tumor, NOS or NEC</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An aggressive malignant embryonal neoplasm arising from the central nervous system. It is composed of cells with a large eccentric nucleus, prominent nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm. Mutations of the SMARCB1 gene or very rarely SMARCA4 (BRG1) gene are present. The vast majority of cases occur in childhood. Symptoms include lethargy, vomiting, cranial nerve palsy, headache, and hemiplegia."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An aggressive malignant embryonal neoplasm arising from the central nervous system. It is composed of cells with a large eccentric nucleus, prominent nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm. Mutations of the SMARCB1 gene or very rarely SMARCA4 (BRG1) gene are present. The vast majority of cases occur in childhood. Symptoms include lethargy, vomiting, cranial nerve palsy, headache, and hemiplegia.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6906"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C6906" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C6906</a></span></td></tr>

The lung is the most frequent site of metastasis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A high grade malignant bone-forming mesenchymal neoplasm producing osteoid. The tumor arises from the medullary portion of the bone. It affects the long bones and most commonly, the distal femur, proximal tibia, and proximal humerus. Pain with or without a palpable mass is the most common clinical presentation. It usually has an aggressive growth and may metastasize through the hematogenous route. The lung is the most frequent site of metastasis.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C35870"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C35870" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C35870</a></span></td></tr>

Most cases have been reported in pediatric patients."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A provisional tumor entity described in the supratentorial brain and characterized by a distinct DNA methylation profile and monosomy of chromosome 14. It is composed of small to medium-sized cells showing perinuclear oligodendroglioma-like haloes, scattered multinucleated cells, and nuclear clusters composed of large pleomorphic nuclei. <tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Diffuse Low-Grade Glioma, MAPK Pathway-Altered"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Diffuse Low-Grade Glioma, MAPK Pathway-Altered" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C185218" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Diffuse Low-Grade Glioma, MAPK Pathway-Altered</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare, low-grade diffuse glioma with morphological features of astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma, generally affecting children. It is characterized by a gene alteration that results in a MAPK pathway abnormality. The genetic abnormalities are typically a BRAF p.V600E substitution mutation, mutations or fusions involving the FGFR1 gene and internal tandem duplication (ITD) of the sequences of FGFR1 gene encoding the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD). The tumor is IDH-wildtype and does not have a homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, low-grade diffuse glioma with morphological features of astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma, generally affecting children. It is characterized by a gene alteration that results in a MAPK pathway abnormality. The genetic abnormalities are typically a BRAF p.V600E substitution mutation, mutations or fusions involving the FGFR1 gene and internal tandem duplication (ITD) of the sequences of FGFR1 gene encoding the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD). The tumor is IDH-wildtype and does not have a homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C185218"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C185218" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C185218</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Diffuse Pediatric-Type High-Grade Glioma, H3-Wildtype And IDH-Wildtype"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Diffuse Pediatric-Type High-Grade Glioma, H3-Wildtype And IDH-Wildtype" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C185467" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Diffuse Pediatric-Type High-Grade Glioma, H3-Wildtype And IDH-Wildtype</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An aggressive, WHO grade 4 diffuse brain glioma usually affecting children, adolescents, or young adults. <tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C27502" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare malignant soft tissue neoplasm of uncertain differentiation, characterized by the presence of chondroblast-like cells in a myxoid stroma and a multinodular growth pattern.  The most common sites of involvement are the deep soft tissues of the extremities, particularly the thigh.  It usually presents as an enlarging soft tissue mass.  Patients may have long survivals, but local recurrences and metastases occur in approximately half of the cases.  The most common site of metastasis is the lungs."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare malignant soft tissue neoplasm of uncertain differentiation, characterized by the presence of chondroblast-like cells in a myxoid stroma and a multinodular growth pattern.  The most common sites of involvement are the deep soft tissues of the extremities, particularly the thigh.  It usually presents as an enlarging soft tissue mass.  Patients may have long survivals, but local recurrences and metastases occur in approximately half of the cases.  The most common site of metastasis is the lungs.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C27502"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C27502" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C27502</a></span></td></tr>

Symptoms include the painless enlargement of lymph nodes, spleen, or other immune tissue. Other symptoms include fever, weight loss, fatigue, or night sweats."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A cancer of the immune system that is marked by the presence of a type of cell called the Reed-Sternberg cell. It includes entities previously termed intracranial angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma or intracranial myxoid mesenchymal tumor. It is usually located in the supratentorial brain and mostly affects children and young adults. There is a spectrum of clinical behaviors ranging from slowly growing tumors to rapid recurrences, and rarely metastases."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A provisional entity that refers to a group of neoplasms with a broad morphological spectrum, characterized by fusion of a FET family gene (usually EWSR1 and rarely FUS) with a member of the CREB family of transcription factors (CREB1, ATF1, or CREM). It includes entities previously termed intracranial angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma or intracranial myxoid mesenchymal tumor. It is usually located in the supratentorial brain and mostly affects children and young adults. <tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Low-Grade Fibromyxoid Sarcoma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Low-Grade Fibromyxoid Sarcoma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C45202" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Low-Grade Fibromyxoid Sarcoma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A low-grade, late-metastasizing variant of fibrosarcoma characterized by alternating fibrous and myxoid areas and a whorling growth pattern.  The neoplastic cells have a spindle morphology, and lack hyperchromasia or significant nuclear atypia.  Approximately 40% of cases show the focal presence of collagen rosettes.  A t(7;16)(q33;p11) translocation has been identified in the majority of cases, associated with the presence of FUS-CREB3L2 fusion protein.  Rare cases carry the t(11;16)(p11;p11) translocation which is associated with the presence of the FUS-CREB3L1 fusion protein."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A low-grade, late-metastasizing variant of fibrosarcoma characterized by alternating fibrous and myxoid areas and a whorling growth pattern.  The neoplastic cells have a spindle morphology, and lack hyperchromasia or significant nuclear atypia.  Approximately 40% of cases show the focal presence of collagen rosettes.  A t(7;16)(q33;p11) translocation has been identified in the majority of cases, associated with the presence of FUS-CREB3L2 fusion protein.  Rare cases carry the t(11;16)(p11;p11) translocation which is associated with the presence of the FUS-CREB3L1 fusion protein.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C45202"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C45202" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C45202</a></span></td></tr>
