<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C7930" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An angiocentric and angiodestructive lymphoproliferative disease involving extranodal sites, comprised of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive B-cells admixed with reactive T-cells.  Incidence is higher among adult males; patients with a history of immunodeficiency are at increased risk.  The most common site of involvement is the lung; other common sites include brain, kidney, liver, and skin.  Morphologically, three grades are recognized: grade I, II, and III.  Grade III lymphomatoid granulomatosis should be approached clinically as a subtype of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An angiocentric and angiodestructive lymphoproliferative disease involving extranodal sites, comprised of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive B-cells admixed with reactive T-cells.  Incidence is higher among adult males; patients with a history of immunodeficiency are at increased risk.  The most common site of involvement is the lung; other common sites include brain, kidney, liver, and skin.  Morphologically, three grades are recognized: grade I, II, and III.  Grade III lymphomatoid granulomatosis should be approached clinically as a subtype of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C7930"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C7930" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C7930</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Meningioma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Meningioma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3230" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Meningioma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A generally slow growing tumor attached to the dura mater. It is composed of neoplastic meningothelial (arachnoidal) cells. It typically occurs in adults, often women and it has a wide range of histopathological appearances. Of the various subtypes, meningothelial, fibrous and transitional meningiomas are the most common. Most meningiomas are WHO grade 1 tumors, and some are WHO grade 2 or 3 tumors. Most subtypes share a common clinical behavior, although some subtypes are more likely to recur and follow a more aggressive clinical course. (Adapted from WHO)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A generally slow growing tumor attached to the dura mater. It is composed of neoplastic meningothelial (arachnoidal) cells. It typically occurs in adults, often women and it has a wide range of histopathological appearances. Of the various subtypes, meningothelial, fibrous and transitional meningiomas are the most common. Most meningiomas are WHO grade 1 tumors, and some are WHO grade 2 or 3 tumors. <tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Myxoid Glioneuronal Tumor"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Myxoid Glioneuronal Tumor" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C179229" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Myxoid Glioneuronal Tumor</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare, low-grade glioneuronal neoplasm characterized by a dinucleotide mutation at codon 385 of the PDGFR gene. It usually occurs in the septum pellucidum. It has also been described in the corpus callosum and periventricular white matter of the lateral ventricle. It has histologic features reminiscent of either dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor or rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor. It is composed of oligodendrocyte-like cells in a prominent myxoid stroma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, low-grade glioneuronal neoplasm characterized by a dinucleotide mutation at codon 385 of the PDGFR gene. It usually occurs in the septum pellucidum. It has also been described in the corpus callosum and periventricular white matter of the lateral ventricle. It has histologic features reminiscent of either dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor or rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor. It is composed of oligodendrocyte-like cells in a prominent myxoid stroma.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C179229"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C179229" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C179229</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Paraganglioma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Paraganglioma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3308" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Paraganglioma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A neoplasm arising from paraganglia located along the sympathetic or parasympathetic nerves.  Infrequently, it may arise outside the usual distribution of the sympathetic and parasympathetic paraganglia.  Tumors arising from the adrenal gland medulla are called pheochromocytomas.  Morphologically, paragangliomas usually display a nesting (Zellballen) growth pattern.  There are no reliable morphologic criteria to distinguish between benign and malignant paragangliomas.  The only definitive indicator of malignancy is the presence of regional or distant metastases."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A neoplasm arising from paraganglia located along the sympathetic or parasympathetic nerves.  Infrequently, it may arise outside the usual distribution of the sympathetic and parasympathetic paraganglia.  Tumors arising from the adrenal gland medulla are called pheochromocytomas.  Morphologically, paragangliomas usually display a nesting (Zellballen) growth pattern.  There are no reliable morphologic criteria to distinguish between benign and malignant paragangliomas.  The only definitive indicator of malignancy is the presence of regional or distant metastases.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3308"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3308" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3308</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Pineal Tumors"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Pineal Tumors" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C41834" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Pineal Tumors</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="The tissue of the pineal gland. The pineal gland is a small reddish-gray body, about 8 mm. in length which lies in the depression between the superior colliculi. It is attached to the roof of the third ventricle near its junction with the mid-brain. It develops as an outgrowth from the third ventricle of the brain. The pineal parenchyma consists of follicles lined by epithelium and enveloped by connective tissues. It produces and secretes melatonin."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The tissue of the pineal gland. The pineal gland is a small reddish-gray body, about 8 mm. in length which lies in the depression between the superior colliculi. It is attached to the roof of the third ventricle near its junction with the mid-brain. It develops as an outgrowth from the third ventricle of the brain. The pineal parenchyma consists of follicles lined by epithelium and enveloped by connective tissues. It produces and secretes melatonin.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C41834"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C41834" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C41834</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Polymorphous Low-Grade Neuroepithelial Tumor Of The Young"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Polymorphous Low-Grade Neuroepithelial Tumor Of The Young" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C180378" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Polymorphous Low-Grade Neuroepithelial Tumor Of The Young</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A low-grade cerebral tumor associated with seizures and in many cases refractory epilepsy. It usually occurs in the second and third decades of life. It is characterized by the presence of oligodendroglioma-like components. It may also contain astrocytic components. MAPK pathway-activating genetic alterations play a role in the development of this tumor. Causative gene alterations include mutations resulting in the expression of BRAF p.V600E and gene fusions involving FGFR2 or FGFR3 genes. IDH gene mutations and 1p/19q codeletion are not present."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A low-grade cerebral tumor associated with seizures and in many cases refractory epilepsy. It usually occurs in the second and third decades of life. It is characterized by the presence of oligodendroglioma-like components. It may also contain astrocytic components. MAPK pathway-activating genetic alterations play a role in the development of this tumor. Causative gene alterations include mutations resulting in the expression of BRAF p.V600E and gene fusions involving FGFR2 or FGFR3 genes. IDH gene mutations and 1p/19q codeletion are not present.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C180378"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C180378" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C180378</a></span></td></tr>

It usually occurs in children younger than five years. PFA ependymomas have a worst prognosis compared to PFB ependymomas."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A circumscribed ependymoma that arises in the posterior fossa with characteristic DNA methylation patterns, including CpG island hypermethylation, global DNA hypomethylation, reduction of nuclear H3 p.K28me3 (K27me3) expression, and EZHIP  overexpression. It usually occurs in children younger than five years. PFA ependymomas have a worst prognosis compared to PFB ependymomas.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C186450"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C186450" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C186450</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Posterior Fossa Ependymoma, Group PFB"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Posterior Fossa Ependymoma, Group PFB" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C186451" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Posterior Fossa Ependymoma, Group PFB</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A circumscribed ependymoma that arises in the posterior fossa with characteristic DNA methylation patterns including retention of nuclear H3 p.K28me3 (K27me3) expression, absence of CpG island hypermethylation, absence of global DNA hypomethylation, and absence of EZHIP overexpression. Widespread cytogenetic abnormalities are present. Frequent chromosomal aberrations include loss of 22q, monosomy 6, and trisomy 18. It occurs in children older than five years and adults and has a relatively good prognosis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A circumscribed ependymoma that arises in the posterior fossa with characteristic DNA methylation patterns including retention of nuclear H3 p.K28me3 (K27me3) expression, absence of CpG island hypermethylation, absence of global DNA hypomethylation, and absence of EZHIP overexpression. Widespread cytogenetic abnormalities are present. Frequent chromosomal aberrations include loss of 22q, monosomy 6, and trisomy 18. It occurs in children older than five years and adults and has a relatively good prognosis.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C186451"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C186451" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C186451</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C121668" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An intermediate, rarely metastasizing blood vessel neoplasm that more frequently affects young adult males and usually arises in the lower limbs.  In approximately half of the affected patients the tumor is painful and in two-thirds of the patients the tumor is multifocal.  Morphologically it is characterized by the presence of sheets and fascicles of spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei.  Cytologic atypia is usually mild.  Approximately 60% of the patients develop local recurrences or additional tumors in the same anatomic region."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An intermediate, rarely metastasizing blood vessel neoplasm that more frequently affects young adult males and usually arises in the lower limbs.  In approximately half of the affected patients the tumor is painful and in two-thirds of the patients the tumor is multifocal.  Morphologically it is characterized by the presence of sheets and fascicles of spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei.  Cytologic atypia is usually mild.  Approximately 60% of the patients develop local recurrences or additional tumors in the same anatomic region.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C121668"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C121668" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C121668</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Rosai-Dorfman Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Rosai-Dorfman Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C36075" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Rosai-Dorfman Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare histiocytic disorder of unknown etiology, characterized by distention of the lymph node sinuses and sinusoidal histiocytic infiltration. The histiocytes characteristically contain ingested lymphocytes and are S100 and CD68 positive, and CD1a negative. Patients present with cervical lymphadenopathy, fever, leukocytosis, and hypergammaglobulinemia. It can affect extranodal sites, including skin, bones, and the respiratory tract. It occurs in isolation or may be associated with autoimmune disorders or malignancies. Mutations in NRAS, KRAS, MAP2K1, and ARAF genes have been identified in affected tissues, suggesting a clonal origin in some cases. It is a self-limited disorder, although some patients may have a poor prognosis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare histiocytic disorder of unknown etiology, characterized by distention of the lymph node sinuses and sinusoidal histiocytic infiltration. The histiocytes characteristically contain ingested lymphocytes and are S100 and CD68 positive, and CD1a negative. Patients present with cervical lymphadenopathy, fever, leukocytosis, and hypergammaglobulinemia. It can affect extranodal sites, including skin, bones, and the respiratory tract. It occurs in isolation or may be associated with autoimmune disorders or malignancies. Mutations in NRAS, KRAS, MAP2K1, and ARAF genes have been identified in affected tissues, suggesting a clonal origin in some cases. It is a self-limited disorder, although some patients may have a poor prognosis.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C36075"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C36075" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C36075</a></span></td></tr>

Somatic mutations can occur in any of the cells of the body except the germ cells (sperm and egg) and therefore are not passed on to children. <tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Spinal Ependymoma, MYCN-Amplified"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Spinal Ependymoma, MYCN-Amplified" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C186494" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Spinal Ependymoma, MYCN-Amplified</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare, aggressive ependymoma that arises from the spinal cord. Cytogenetic abnormalities include loss of chromosome 10 and focal losses on chromosome 11q. The prognosis is poor."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, aggressive ependymoma that arises from the spinal cord. It displays microvascular proliferation, necrosis, and high mitotic rate. It is characterized by high-level MYCN amplification. <tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Synovial Sarcoma, NOS"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Synovial Sarcoma, NOS" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3400" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Synovial Sarcoma, NOS</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A malignant neoplasm characterized by the chromosomal translocation t(X;18)(p11;q11).  It can occur at any age, but mainly affects young adults, more commonly males.  Although any site can be affected, the vast majority of the cases arise in the deep soft tissues of extremities, especially around the knee.  Microscopically, synovial sarcoma is classified as monophasic (with a spindle or epithelial cell component) or biphasic (with both spindle and epithelial cell components).  Synovial sarcomas can recur or metastasize to the lungs, bones, and lymph nodes."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A malignant neoplasm characterized by the chromosomal translocation t(X;18)(p11;q11).  It can occur at any age, but mainly affects young adults, more commonly males.  Although any site can be affected, the vast majority of the cases arise in the deep soft tissues of extremities, especially around the knee.  Microscopically, synovial sarcoma is classified as monophasic (with a spindle or epithelial cell component) or biphasic (with both spindle and epithelial cell components).  Synovial sarcomas can recur or metastasize to the lungs, bones, and lymph nodes.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3400"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3400" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3400</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor Localized Type"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor Localized Type" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6532" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor Localized Type</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A well-circumscribed, lobulated tumor, completely or partially covered by a fibrous capsule. The tumor is slow-growing, usually developing over several years. It usually arises in the fingers.  It is characterized by the presence of mononuclear cells, multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells, hemosiderin-laden macrophages, foam cells, and an inflammatory infiltrate. Patients may present with disseminated intravascular coagulation.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C82403"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C82403" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C82403</a></span></td></tr>

After age 4 this is no longer the case."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Acute myeloid leukemia occurring in children with Down syndrome. During the first 3 years of life, it is usually the megakaryoblastic subtype, and is associated with GATA1 gene mutation. After age 4 this is no longer the case.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C43223"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C43223" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C43223</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="WHO, Version 4 &gt;&gt; Myeloid Proliferations Related to Down Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="WHO, Version 4 &gt;&gt; Myeloid Proliferations Related to Down Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C82338" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>WHO, Version 4 &gt;&gt; Myeloid Proliferations Related to Down Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="Hematologic neoplasms occurring in individuals with Down syndrome.  There is an increased risk of acute leukemias in both children and adults with Down syndrome.  In particular, the incidence of acute myeloid leukemia in Down syndrome children of less than five years of age is particularly high, it is usually an acute megakaryoblastic leukemia, and is associated with GATA1 gene mutation.  This group of disorders also includes the entity transient abnormal myelopoiesis which occurs in neonates and is associated with GATA1 gene mutation."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hematologic neoplasms occurring in individuals with Down syndrome.  There is an increased risk of acute leukemias in both children and adults with Down syndrome.  In particular, the incidence of acute myeloid leukemia in Down syndrome children of less than five years of age is particularly high, it is usually an acute megakaryoblastic leukemia, and is associated with GATA1 gene mutation.  This group of disorders also includes the entity transient abnormal myelopoiesis which occurs in neonates and is associated with GATA1 gene mutation.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C82338"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C82338" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C82338</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base fprh pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Acetabulum"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Acetabulum" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C32042" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Acetabulum</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="The acetabulum is a concave surface of the pelvis. The head of the femur meets with the pelvis at the acetabulum, forming the hip joint. There are three bones of the os coxae (hip bone) that come together to form the acetabulum. Contributing a little more than two-fifths of the structure is the ischium, which provides lower and side boundaries to the acetabulum. The ilium forms the upper boundary, providing a little less than two-fifths of the structure of the acetabulum. The rest is formed by the pubis, near the midline. It is bounded by a prominent uneven rim, which is thick and strong above, and serves for the attachment of the acetabular labrum, which reduces its opening, and deepens the surface for formation of the hip joint. At the lower part of the acetabulum is the acetabular notch, which is continuous with a circular depression, the acetabular fossa, at the bottom of the cavity of the acetabulum. The rest of the acetabulum is formed by a curved, crescent-moon shaped surface, the lunate surface, where the joint is made with the head of the femur. Its counterpart in the pectoral girdle is the glenoid fossa."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The acetabulum is a concave surface of the pelvis. The head of the femur meets with the pelvis at the acetabulum, forming the hip joint. There are three bones of the os coxae (hip bone) that come together to form the acetabulum. Contributing a little more than two-fifths of the structure is the ischium, which provides lower and side boundaries to the acetabulum. The ilium forms the upper boundary, providing a little less than two-fifths of the structure of the acetabulum. The rest is formed by the pubis, near the midline. It is bounded by a prominent uneven rim, which is thick and strong above, and serves for the attachment of the acetabular labrum, which reduces its opening, and deepens the surface for formation of the hip joint. At the lower part of the acetabulum is the acetabular notch, which is continuous with a circular depression, the acetabular fossa, at the bottom of the cavity of the acetabulum. The rest of the acetabulum is formed by a curved, crescent-moon shaped surface, the lunate surface, where the joint is made with the head of the femur. Its counterpart in the pectoral girdle is the glenoid fossa.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C32042"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C32042" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C32042</a></span></td></tr>

Its function is to expel feces, unwanted semi-solid matter produced during digestion, which, depending on the type of animal, may be one or more of: matter which the animal cannot digest, such as bones; food material after all the nutrients have been extracted, for example cellulose or lignin; ingested matter which would be toxic if it remained in the digestive tract; and dead or excess gut bacteria and other endosymbionts."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Orifice at the opposite end of an animal's digestive tract from the mouth. Its function is to expel feces, unwanted semi-solid matter produced during digestion, which, depending on the type of animal, may be one or more of: matter which the animal cannot digest, such as bones; food material after all the nutrients have been extracted, for example cellulose or lignin; ingested matter which would be toxic if it remained in the digestive tract; and dead or excess gut bacteria and other endosymbionts.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C43362"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C43362" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C43362</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base fprh nrsts pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Hip"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Hip" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C64193" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hip</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="The hip region is located lateral to the gluteal region (i.e. the buttock), inferior to the iliac crest, and overlying the greater trochanter of the thigh bone. In adults, three of the bones of the pelvis have fused into the hip bone which forms part of the hip region. The hip joint, scientifically referred to as the acetabulofemoral joint (art. coxae), is the joint between the femur and acetabulum of the pelvis and its primary function is to support the weight of the body in both static (e.g. standing) and dynamic (e.g. walking or running) postures."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The hip region is located lateral to the gluteal region (i.e. the buttock), inferior to the iliac crest, and overlying the greater trochanter of the thigh bone. In adults, three of the bones of the pelvis have fused into the hip bone which forms part of the hip region. The hip joint, scientifically referred to as the acetabulofemoral joint (art. coxae), is the joint between the femur and acetabulum of the pelvis and its primary function is to support the weight of the body in both static (e.g. standing) and dynamic (e.g. walking or running) postures.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C64193"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C64193" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C64193</a></span></td></tr>

The buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Anatomical cavity at the start of the digestive tract that that is enclosed by the mouth. The boundaries and contents vary depending on the species. In vertebrates, the boundaries are the oral opening, the cheeks, the palate and (if present) the palatoglossal arch - if this is not present then the mouth and pharynx form the oropharyngeal cavity. The buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present).</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C12421"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C12421" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C12421</a></span></td></tr>

It is located in the upper anterior portion of the chest, behind the sternum. It is composed predominantly of lymphocytes and fewer epithelial cells. Connective tissue septa separate the lobes into lobules. The lobules contain an outer portion (cortical zone) which is rich in lymphocytes and an inner portion (medullary zone) which is rich in epithelial cells. It is an organ essential for the development of the immune system. Its function is the maturation of the progenitor lymphoid cells to thymocytes and subsequently to mature T-cells. It reaches its greatest weight at puberty and subsequently begins to involute."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A bi-lobed organ surrounded by a connective tissue capsule. It is located in the upper anterior portion of the chest, behind the sternum. It is composed predominantly of lymphocytes and fewer epithelial cells. Connective tissue septa separate the lobes into lobules. The lobules contain an outer portion (cortical zone) which is rich in lymphocytes and an inner portion (medullary zone) which is rich in epithelial cells. It is an organ essential for the development of the immune system. Its function is the maturation of the progenitor lymphoid cells to thymocytes and subsequently to mature T-cells. It reaches its greatest weight at puberty and subsequently begins to involute.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C12433"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C12433" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C12433</a></span></td></tr>

Methamphetamine acts by both facilitating the release of catecholamines, particularly noradrenaline, dopamine and serotonin, from nerve terminals in the brain and by inhibiting their uptake. This leads to an increase in synaptic concentration of these neurotransmitters and results in increased stimulation of postsynaptic receptors.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C61840"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C61840" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C61840</a></span></td></tr>

Strabismus is caused by an imbalance in the extraocular muscles which control the positioning of the eyes. Strabismus is normal in newborns but should resolve by the time the baby is 6 months old. In older children with strabismus, the brain may learn to ignore the input from one eye, and this may lead to amblyopia, a potentially permanent decrease in vision in that eye if not corrected."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Strabismus is the intermittent or constant misalignment of an eye so that its line of vision is not pointed at the same object as the other eye. Strabismus is caused by an imbalance in the extraocular muscles which control the positioning of the eyes. Strabismus is normal in newborns but should resolve by the time the baby is 6 months old. In older children with strabismus, the brain may learn to ignore the input from one eye, and this may lead to amblyopia, a potentially permanent decrease in vision in that eye if not corrected.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C35040"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C35040" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C35040</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Sequencing, NGS, ATAC-seq"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Sequencing, NGS, ATAC-seq" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C156056" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Sequencing, NGS, ATAC-seq</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A molecular genetic technique that isolates and sequences chromosomal regions that are rich in open chromatin. First, nuclei are harvested from a cellular sample. Then a hyperactive Tn5 transposase is added to the nuclei where it excises non-nucleosomal DNA strands and ligates co-administered high-throughput sequencing adapters (tagmentation).  The tagged DNA fragments are isolated, amplified by PCR and sequenced. The number of reads for specific region of DNA correlate with increased chromatin accessibility and this method can identify regions of transcription factor and nucleosome binding."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A molecular genetic technique that isolates and sequences chromosomal regions that are rich in open chromatin. First, nuclei are harvested from a cellular sample. Then a hyperactive Tn5 transposase is added to the nuclei where it excises non-nucleosomal DNA strands and ligates co-administered high-throughput sequencing adapters (tagmentation).  The tagged DNA fragments are isolated, amplified by PCR and sequenced. The number of reads for specific region of DNA correlate with increased chromatin accessibility and this method can identify regions of transcription factor and nucleosome binding.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C156056"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C156056" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C156056</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Sequencing, NGS, Long-Read, Nanopore"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Sequencing, NGS, Long-Read, Nanopore" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C146818" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Sequencing, NGS, Long-Read, Nanopore</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A proprietary next-generation DNA sequencing technology from Oxford Nanopore Technologies that can directly identify and sequence a DNA molecule as it passes through a nanopore, driven by electrophoresis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A proprietary next-generation DNA sequencing technology from Oxford Nanopore Technologies that can directly identify and sequence a DNA molecule as it passes through a nanopore, driven by electrophoresis.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C146818"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C146818" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C146818</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Sequencing, NGS, Long-Read, SMRT"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Sequencing, NGS, Long-Read, SMRT" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C146819" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Sequencing, NGS, Long-Read, SMRT</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A proprietary third-generation DNA sequencing system from Pacific Biosciences that uses zero-mode waveguides (ZMWs) and phospholinked nucleotides. A single DNA polymerase enzyme is affixed at the bottom of a ZMW structure with a single molecule of DNA as a template. A fluorescent tag is cleaved off with each base addition and is detected to create the sequence."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A proprietary third-generation DNA sequencing system from Pacific Biosciences that uses zero-mode waveguides (ZMWs) and phospholinked nucleotides. This system can help determine the likelihood of preserving the vision while the tumor is being treated. It is divided into 5 stages, and each stage predicts the potential to save the eye with external beam radiation therapy. Today, radiation therapy is reserved as a last resort to save a second eye, when all other treatments have failed. As a result, the Reese-Ellsworth classification is now rarely used."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A staging system for intraocular retinoblastoma that was developed in the 1960s, when children were treated with external beam radiation therapy. This system can help determine the likelihood of preserving the vision while the tumor is being treated. It is divided into 5 stages, and each stage predicts the potential to save the eye with external beam radiation therapy. Today, radiation therapy is reserved as a last resort to save a second eye, when all other treatments have failed. As a result, the Reese-Ellsworth classification is now rarely used.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C123333"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C123333" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C123333</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Obstructive Lung Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Obstructive Lung Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3199" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Obstructive Lung Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3199"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3199" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3199</a></span></td></tr>

Osteoporosis is classified as primary (Type 1, postmenopausal osteoporosis; Type 2, age-associated osteoporosis; and idiopathic, which can affect juveniles, premenopausal women, and middle-aged men) and secondary osteoporosis (which results from an identifiable cause of bone mass loss)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition of reduced bone mass, with decreased cortical thickness and a decrease in the number and size of the trabeculae of cancellous bone (but normal chemical composition), resulting in increased fracture incidence. Osteoporosis is classified as primary (Type 1, postmenopausal osteoporosis; Type 2, age-associated osteoporosis; and idiopathic, which can affect juveniles, premenopausal women, and middle-aged men) and secondary osteoporosis (which results from an identifiable cause of bone mass loss).</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3298"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3298" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3298</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Attenuated Familial Adenomatous Polyposis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Attenuated Familial Adenomatous Polyposis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6729" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Attenuated Familial Adenomatous Polyposis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare genetic syndrome with an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance. It is most commonly associated with mutations in the APC gene specifically: exons 1-5, exon 9 and in the distal 3' terminus. Clinical presentation occurs in the middle decades and is characterized by the proximal development of multiple (but less than 100), non-polypoid colonic adenomas. Clinical progression to colorectal cancer may occur later in life but the risk is less than with classic FAP."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare genetic syndrome with an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance. It was formerly called hereditary flat adenoma syndrome (HFAS) but is now recognized as an attenuated variant of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). It is most commonly associated with mutations in the APC gene specifically: exons 1-5, exon 9 and in the distal 3' terminus. Clinical presentation occurs in the middle decades and is characterized by the proximal development of multiple (but less than 100), non-polypoid colonic adenomas. Clinical progression to colorectal cancer may occur later in life but the risk is less than with classic FAP.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6729"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C6729" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C6729</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34415" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A complex syndrome resulting from various genetic and epigenetic anomalies of the 11p15.5 chromosomal region, leading to dysregulated expression of imprinted genes. Specific genes involved include CDKN1C, H19, IGF2, and KCNQ1OT1. One of the key genetic anomalies is an imbalance between the paternally expressed IGF2 growth enhancer gene and the maternally expressed H19 growth suppressor gene, leading to fetal and postnatal overgrowth. The condition is typically characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, umbilical hernia or more severe abdominal wall anomalies such as omphalocele, ear lobe indentations, and hypoglycemia associated with hyperinsulinemia due to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia. Patients with this syndrome have an increased risk for development of embryonal tumors (particularly Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma) and adrenal cortex carcinoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A complex syndrome resulting from various genetic and epigenetic anomalies of the 11p15.5 chromosomal region, leading to dysregulated expression of imprinted genes. The condition is typically characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, umbilical hernia or more severe abdominal wall anomalies such as omphalocele, ear lobe indentations, and hypoglycemia associated with hyperinsulinemia due to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia. Patients with this syndrome have an increased risk for development of embryonal tumors (particularly Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma) and adrenal cortex carcinoma.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34415"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C34415" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C34415</a></span></td></tr>

It is caused by a mutation in the FLCN gene which encodes the protein folliculin. Clinical signs include multiple benign growths of the skin and lungs that begin to manifest in the second or third decade of life. The clinical course is characterized by the progressive growth of new and existing neoplasms. In those with mutations in both copies of FLCN, the kidneys may also be affected by the growth of benign or malignant neoplasms."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare genetic syndrome with an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance. It is caused by a mutation in the FLCN gene which encodes the protein folliculin. Clinical signs include multiple benign growths of the skin and lungs that begin to manifest in the second or third decade of life. The clinical course is characterized by the progressive growth of new and existing neoplasms. <tr data-subsets="base os pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bloom Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bloom Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2903" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bloom Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare, inherited disorder marked by height that is shorter than average, a narrow face with redness and a rash, a high-pitched voice, and fertility problems. Patients with this disorder have an increased risk of cancer, especially leukemia and osteosarcoma (bone cancer). Bloom syndrome is caused by changes in a protein that normally helps cells make copies of the DNA. Changes in this protein cause many breaks, rearrangements, and other mutations in the DNA. It is a type of autosomal recessive genetic disease."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, inherited disorder marked by height that is shorter than average, a narrow face with redness and a rash, a high-pitched voice, and fertility problems. Patients with this disorder have an increased risk of cancer, especially leukemia and osteosarcoma (bone cancer). Bloom syndrome is caused by changes in a protein that normally helps cells make copies of the DNA. Changes in this protein cause many breaks, rearrangements, and other mutations in the DNA. It is a type of autosomal recessive genetic disease.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2903"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C2903" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C2903</a></span></td></tr>

It is the most common malignant tumor in females. Risk factors include country of birth, family history, menstrual and reproductive history, fibrocystic disease and epithelial hyperplasia, exogenous estrogens, contraceptive agents, and ionizing radiation. The vast majority of breast carcinomas are adenocarcinomas (ductal or lobular). Breast carcinoma spreads by direct invasion, by the lymphatic route, and by the blood vessel route. The most common site of lymph node involvement is the axilla."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A carcinoma arising from the breast, most commonly the terminal ductal-lobular unit. It is the most common malignant tumor in females. Risk factors include country of birth, family history, menstrual and reproductive history, fibrocystic disease and epithelial hyperplasia, exogenous estrogens, contraceptive agents, and ionizing radiation. The vast majority of breast carcinomas are adenocarcinomas (ductal or lobular). Breast carcinoma spreads by direct invasion, by the lymphatic route, and by the blood vessel route. The most common site of lymph node involvement is the axilla.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C4872"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C4872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C4872</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C115207" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare, autosomal recessive inherited disorder caused by mutation in the c-Mpl gene. <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Constitutional Mismatch Repair Deficiency"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Constitutional Mismatch Repair Deficiency" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C130202" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Constitutional Mismatch Repair Deficiency</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare childhood cancer predisposition syndrome caused by biallelic inheritance of mutations in MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2 genes. It is characterized by the development of childhood cancers, usually hematological malignancies and/or brain tumors, and colorectal cancers with multiple intestinal polyps. The majority of patients show signs of neurofibromatosis type 1."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare childhood cancer predisposition syndrome caused by biallelic inheritance of mutations in MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2 genes. It is characterized by the development of childhood cancers, usually hematological malignancies and/or brain tumors, and colorectal cancers with multiple intestinal polyps. The majority of patients show signs of neurofibromatosis type 1.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C130202"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C130202" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C130202</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Costello Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Costello Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84652" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Costello Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A genetic syndrome caused by mutations in the HRAS gene. It is characterized by developmental delay, mental retardation, loose skin folds, cardiomyopathy, tachycardia, and structural heart defects. Patients are at an increased risk of developing benign or malignant neoplasms."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A genetic syndrome caused by mutations in the HRAS gene. It is characterized by developmental delay, mental retardation, loose skin folds, cardiomyopathy, tachycardia, and structural heart defects. Patients are at an increased risk of developing benign or malignant neoplasms.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84652"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C84652" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C84652</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cowden Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cowden Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3076" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cowden Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant hereditary syndrome characterized by a variety of hamartomas and neoplasms including verrucous skin lesions, fibromas of the oral cavity, facial trichilemmomas, hamartomatous colonic polyps, thyroid neoplasms, breast cancer, and dysplastic gangliocytomas of the cerebellum."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant hereditary syndrome characterized by a variety of hamartomas and neoplasms including verrucous skin lesions, fibromas of the oral cavity, facial trichilemmomas, hamartomatous colonic polyps, thyroid neoplasms, breast cancer, and dysplastic gangliocytomas of the cerebellum.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3076"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3076" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3076</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cushing Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cushing Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2969" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cushing Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A clinical condition characterized by variable degrees of central obesity, rounding of the face (&quot;moon&quot; face), hypertension, striae, and a number of other physical findings, as a result of prolonged exposure to supranormal cortisol concentration of any etiology."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A clinical condition characterized by variable degrees of central obesity, rounding of the face ("moon" face), hypertension, striae, and a number of other physical findings, as a result of prolonged exposure to supranormal cortisol concentration of any etiology.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2969"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C2969" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C2969</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="DICER1 Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="DICER1 Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C123317" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>DICER1 Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant inherited tumor predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations of the DICER1 gene. Carriers are at an increased risk of developing benign and malignant neoplasms, including pleuropulmonary blastoma, childhood cystic nephroma, goiter, thyroid carcinoma, pineoblastoma, DICER1-mutant ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, and primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant inherited tumor predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations of the DICER1 gene. Carriers are at an increased risk of developing benign and malignant neoplasms, including pleuropulmonary blastoma, childhood cystic nephroma, goiter, thyroid carcinoma, pineoblastoma, DICER1-mutant ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, and primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1-mutant.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C123317"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C123317" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C123317</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Denys-Drash Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Denys-Drash Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84668" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Denys-Drash Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A Wilms tumor 1 gene syndrome caused by various point mutation(s) affecting the zinc finger(s) of the Wilms tumor protein. This syndrome is characterized by congenital nephropathy (diffuse mesangial sclerosis), gonadal dysgenesis resulting in atypical genital and reproductive tract development in male infants, and high risk for development of Wilms tumor, an embryonal neoplasm defined by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A Wilms tumor 1 gene syndrome caused by various point mutation(s) affecting the zinc finger(s) of the Wilms tumor protein. This syndrome is characterized by congenital nephropathy (diffuse mesangial sclerosis), gonadal dysgenesis resulting in atypical genital and reproductive tract development in male infants, and high risk for development of Wilms tumor, an embryonal neoplasm defined by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84668"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C84668" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C84668</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Diabetes Mellitus (Type I)"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Diabetes Mellitus (Type I)" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2986" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Diabetes Mellitus (Type I)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chronic condition characterized by minimal or absent production of insulin by the pancreas."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chronic condition characterized by minimal or absent production of insulin by the pancreas.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2986"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C2986" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C2986</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base os pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Diamond-Blackfan Anemia"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Diamond-Blackfan Anemia" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C61236" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Diamond-Blackfan Anemia</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A very rare disorder in which the bone marrow doesn't make enough red blood cells. It is usually seen in the first year of life. Patients may have deformed thumbs and other physical problems. They also have an increased risk of leukemia and sarcoma, especially osteosarcoma (bone cancer). Patients with congenital pure red cell aplasia may have a mutation (change) in one of the genes that make proteins found in the cell's ribosomes."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A very rare disorder in which the bone marrow doesn't make enough red blood cells. It is usually seen in the first year of life. Patients may have deformed thumbs and other physical problems. They also have an increased risk of leukemia and sarcoma, especially osteosarcoma (bone cancer). Patients with congenital pure red cell aplasia may have a mutation (change) in one of the genes that make proteins found in the cell's ribosomes.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C61236"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C61236" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C61236</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl rb"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Down Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Down Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2993" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Down Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chromosomal dysgenesis syndrome resulting from a triplication or translocation of chromosome 21. Down syndrome occurs in approximately 1:700 live births. Abnormalities are variable from individual to individual and may include mental retardation, retarded growth, flat hypoplastic face with short nose, prominent epicanthic skin folds, small low-set ears with prominent antihelix, fissured and thickened tongue, laxness of joint ligaments, pelvic dysplasia, broad hands and feet, stubby fingers, transverse palmar crease, lenticular opacities and heart disease. Patients with Down syndrome have an estimated 10 to 30-fold increased risk for leukemia; most have symptoms of Alzheimer's disease by age 40. Also known as trisomy 21 syndrome."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chromosomal dysgenesis syndrome resulting from a triplication or translocation of chromosome 21. Down syndrome occurs in approximately 1:700 live births. Abnormalities are variable from individual to individual and may include mental retardation, retarded growth, flat hypoplastic face with short nose, prominent epicanthic skin folds, small low-set ears with prominent antihelix, fissured and thickened tongue, laxness of joint ligaments, pelvic dysplasia, broad hands and feet, stubby fingers, transverse palmar crease, lenticular opacities and heart disease. Patients with Down syndrome have an estimated 10 to 30-fold increased risk for leukemia; most have symptoms of Alzheimer's disease by age 40. Also known as trisomy 21 syndrome.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2993"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C2993" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C2993</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Dyskeratosis Congenita"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Dyskeratosis Congenita" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C111802" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Dyskeratosis Congenita</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare genetic disorder characterized by nail dystrophy, reticulated skin pigmentation especially on the neck and chest, and oral leukoplakia.  In about half the cases mutations in the TERT, TERC, DKC1, or TINF2 genes are identified.  Patients are at an increased risk of developing bone marrow failure, myelodysplastic syndrome, leukemia, or cancer, especially in the head and neck region."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare genetic disorder characterized by nail dystrophy, reticulated skin pigmentation especially on the neck and chest, and oral leukoplakia.  In about half the cases mutations in the TERT, TERC, DKC1, or TINF2 genes are identified.  Patients are at an increased risk of developing bone marrow failure, myelodysplastic syndrome, leukemia, or cancer, especially in the head and neck region.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C111802"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C111802" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C111802</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="ETV6-Related Thrombocytopenia and Leukemia Predisposition"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="ETV6-Related Thrombocytopenia and Leukemia Predisposition" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C178386" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>ETV6-Related Thrombocytopenia and Leukemia Predisposition</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant condition caused by mutation(s) in the ETV6 gene, encoding transcription factor ETV6. It is characterized by an increased risk of developing thrombocytopenia and diverse hematologic malignancies, including myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, B lymphoblastic leukemia, and plasma cell myeloma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant condition caused by mutation(s) in the ETV6 gene, encoding transcription factor ETV6. It is characterized by an increased risk of developing thrombocytopenia and diverse hematologic malignancies, including myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, B lymphoblastic leukemia, and plasma cell myeloma.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C178386"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C178386" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C178386</a></span></td></tr>
