<tr data-subsets="base lt pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Familial Adenomatous Polyposis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Familial Adenomatous Polyposis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3339" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Familial Adenomatous Polyposis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant disorder, characterized by the presence of multiple adenomas in the colon and rectum. It is caused by a germline mutation in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene which is located on the long arm of chromosome 5. The adenomas are most often tubular, and they have the tendency to progress to adenocarcinoma. They can occur throughout the colon, but they tend to concentrate in the rectum and sigmoid colon. The colorectal adenomas are detected during endoscopic examination between the age of 10 and 20 years. The adenomas increase in size and numbers with age, and there is usually progression of one or more adenomas to adenocarcinoma. The mean age of development of adenocarcinoma is about 40 years. Signs include rectal bleeding and mucousy diarrhea."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant disorder, characterized by the presence of multiple adenomas in the colon and rectum. It is caused by a germline mutation in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene which is located on the long arm of chromosome 5. The adenomas are most often tubular, and they have the tendency to progress to adenocarcinoma. They can occur throughout the colon, but they tend to concentrate in the rectum and sigmoid colon. The colorectal adenomas are detected during endoscopic examination between the age of 10 and 20 years. The adenomas increase in size and numbers with age, and there is usually progression of one or more adenomas to adenocarcinoma. The mean age of development of adenocarcinoma is about 40 years. Signs include rectal bleeding and mucousy diarrhea.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3339"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3339" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3339</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Familial Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Familial Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C176906" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Familial Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the KIT or PDGFRA genes, encoding mast/stem cell growth factor receptor Kit and platelet derived growth factor receptor alpha respectively. The condition is characterized by the occurrence of multiple gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the KIT or PDGFRA genes, encoding mast/stem cell growth factor receptor Kit and platelet derived growth factor receptor alpha respectively. The condition is characterized by the occurrence of multiple gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST).</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C176906"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C176906" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C176906</a></span></td></tr>

Multiple genes are responsible for Fanconi anemia."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chromosomal instability syndrome that is the most common form of inherited aplastic anemia. It is inherited as an autosomal recessive or X-linked disorder. It is more common in females and can run in families."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autoimmune condition of the thyroid gland (a gland located beneath the larynx). It is caused by the formation of antibodies that attack the thyroid gland and it usually causes hypothyroidism (too little thyroid hormone). Symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, constipation, dry skin, depression, and the inability to exercise. <tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Klinefelter Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Klinefelter Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34752" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Klinefelter Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A condition caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome resulting in 47,XXY karyotype in an individual with male phenotype. The condition is characterized in childhood by relative tall stature with disproportionately long limbs, and speech/language developmental problems in some patients. Postpubertal findings include small testes, gynecomastia, and infertility."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome resulting in 47,XXY karyotype in an individual with male phenotype. The condition is characterized in childhood by relative tall stature with disproportionately long limbs, and speech/language developmental problems in some patients. Postpubertal findings include small testes, gynecomastia, and infertility.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34752"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C34752" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C34752</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="LEOPARD Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="LEOPARD Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84820" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>LEOPARD Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A genetic syndrome caused by mutation(s) in the PTPN11, RAF1, or the BRAF genes, encoding tyrosine-protein phosphatase non-receptor type 11 and RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase, and serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf, respectively. Affected male individuals may exhibit unilateral or bilateral cryptorchidism, small penis, and/or hypospadias (urinary meatus on the dorsal side of the penis). Affected female individuals may have ovarian hypoplasia or agenesis. Primary hypogonadism in both female and male individuals may result in delayed puberty."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A genetic syndrome caused by mutation(s) in the PTPN11, RAF1, or the BRAF genes, encoding tyrosine-protein phosphatase non-receptor type 11 and RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase, and serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf, respectively. Affected male individuals may exhibit unilateral or bilateral cryptorchidism, small penis, and/or hypospadias (urinary meatus on the dorsal side of the penis). Affected female individuals may have ovarian hypoplasia or agenesis. Primary hypogonadism in both female and male individuals may result in delayed puberty.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84820"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C84820" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C84820</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Legius Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Legius Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C176941" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Legius Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the SPRED1 gene, encoding sprouty-related, EVH1 domain-containing protein 1. The condition resembles neurofibromatosis type I but is less severe. Metastatic carcinomas to the lung are also common, and can be difficult to distinguish from primary tumors."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A carcinoma originating in the lung. Lung carcinomas usually arise from the epithelium that lines the bronchial tree (bronchogenic carcinomas), and are classified as small cell or non-small cell carcinomas. Non-small cell lung carcinomas are usually adenocarcinomas, squamous cell carcinomas, or large cell carcinomas. Metastatic carcinomas to the lung are also common, and can be difficult to distinguish from primary tumors.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C4878"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C4878" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C4878</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base ews os pre hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Lynch Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Lynch Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C8494" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Lynch Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant hereditary neoplastic syndrome characterized by the development of colorectal carcinoma and a high risk of developing endometrial carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, and small intestinal carcinoma. Patients often develop colorectal carcinomas at an early age (mean, 45 years). In the majority of the cases the lesions arise from the proximal colon. At the molecular level, high-frequency microsatellite instability is present."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant hereditary neoplastic syndrome characterized by the development of colorectal carcinoma and a high risk of developing endometrial carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, and small intestinal carcinoma. Patients often develop colorectal carcinomas at an early age (mean, 45 years). In the majority of the cases the lesions arise from the proximal colon. At the molecular level, high-frequency microsatellite instability is present.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C8494"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C8494" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C8494</a></span></td></tr>

Clinical course is progressive with variable development of associated malignancies."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare non-inherited disorder primarily affecting the skin and skeletal system. Other clinical features may include hyperthyroidism, goiter, thyroid nodules, hyperadrenocorticolism, growth hormone excess, and phosphate wasting."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A syndrome caused by activating somatic mutation(s) in the GNAS gene, encoding guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(s) subunit alpha isoforms short. This syndrome is characterized most commonly by irregular (coast of Maine) cafe-au-lait skin pigmentation, polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, and gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty due to primary gonadal hyperfunction. This condition is associated with characteristic facial features, including hypertelorism, pubertal delay, occasional progressive cardiomyopathy, insulin resistance with type 2 diabetes, and an increased risk for Wilms tumor."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutation(s) in the TRIM37 gene, encoding E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase TRIM37. Mulibrey is a contraction of muscle, liver, brain, and eyes. "Nanism" is a synonym for "dwarfism". This condition is associated with characteristic facial features, including hypertelorism, pubertal delay, occasional progressive cardiomyopathy, insulin resistance with type 2 diabetes, and an increased risk for Wilms tumor.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84906"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C84906" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C84906</a></span></td></tr>

These tumors are usually benign (not cancer). In some cases, tumors inside the pancreas can become malignant (cancer)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, inherited disorder that affects the endocrine glands and can cause tumors in the parathyroid and pituitary glands and the pancreas. These tumors are usually benign (not cancer). <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C4692" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A disorder, wherein unstable chromosomes have a tendency to break and become rearranged, characterized by microcephaly, stunted growth, subnormal mental development, cafe-au-lait spots, and immunodeficiency. (JABL99)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A disorder, wherein unstable chromosomes have a tendency to break and become rearranged, characterized by microcephaly, stunted growth, subnormal mental development, cafe-au-lait spots, and immunodeficiency. The syndrome is named after the University of Nijmegen in the Netherlands. (JABL99)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C4692"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C4692" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C4692</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Noonan Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Noonan Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34854" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Noonan Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A genetic syndrome caused by mutations in the PTPN11 gene (greater than 50% of the cases) or less frequently mutations in the SOS1, RAF1, or KRAS genes. It is characterized by short stature, webbed neck, hypertelorism, low-set ears, deafness, and thrombocytopenia or abnormal platelet function."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A genetic syndrome caused by mutations in the PTPN11 gene (greater than 50% of the cases) or less frequently mutations in the SOS1, RAF1, or KRAS genes. It is characterized by short stature, webbed neck, hypertelorism, low-set ears, deafness, and thrombocytopenia or abnormal platelet function.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34854"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C34854" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C34854</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Noonan Syndrome-Like Disorder with Loose Anagen Hair"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Noonan Syndrome-Like Disorder with Loose Anagen Hair" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C178129" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Noonan Syndrome-Like Disorder with Loose Anagen Hair</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the SHOC2 or PPP1CB genes, encoding leucine-rich repeat protein SHOC-2 and serine/threonine-protein phosphatase PP1-beta catalytic subunit, respectively. The condition is characterized by facial features similar to those seen in Noonan syndrome but may also include short stature, cognitive deficits, relative macrocephaly, small posterior fossa resulting in Chiari I malformation, hypernasal voice, cardiac defects, and ectodermal abnormalities, which typically presents as slow-growing, sparse, and/or unruly hair."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An inherited condition caused by autosomal dominant mutation(s) in the SHOC2 or PPP1CB genes, encoding leucine-rich repeat protein SHOC-2 and serine/threonine-protein phosphatase PP1-beta catalytic subunit, respectively. The condition is characterized by facial features similar to those seen in Noonan syndrome but may also include short stature, cognitive deficits, relative macrocephaly, small posterior fossa resulting in Chiari I malformation, hypernasal voice, cardiac defects, and ectodermal abnormalities, which typically presents as slow-growing, sparse, and/or unruly hair.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C178129"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C178129" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C178129</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Oculocutaneous Albinism"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Oculocutaneous Albinism" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84941" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Oculocutaneous Albinism</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal recessive inherited disorder caused by mutations of the OCA2, SLC45A2, TYR and TYRP1 genes. It is characterized by hypopigmentation of the skin, hair, and eyes, resulting in very fair skin, white colored hair, and reduced pigmentation in the iris and retina. Individuals may have vision disturbances and photophobia."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal recessive inherited disorder caused by mutations of the OCA2, SLC45A2, TYR and TYRP1 genes. It is characterized by hypopigmentation of the skin, hair, and eyes, resulting in very fair skin, white colored hair, and reduced pigmentation in the iris and retina. Individuals may have vision disturbances and photophobia.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84941"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C84941" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C84941</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base os"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Ollier Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Ollier Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3008" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Ollier Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A rare benign disorder characterized by lack of normal endochondral ossification, and the growth of multiple enchondromas. Extent of the disease varies; in some cases, neoplastic involvement may be widespread causing considerable deformity."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare benign disorder characterized by lack of normal endochondral ossification, and the growth of multiple enchondromas.  It primarily affects the bones of the hand, in children and young adults.  Extent of the disease varies; in some cases, neoplastic involvement may be widespread causing considerable deformity.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3008"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3008" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3008</a></span></td></tr>

Patients with this type of tyrosinemia may also have a predisposition for hepatocellular carcinoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Tyrosinemia caused by mutations in the FAH gene. It is characterized by deficiency of the enzyme fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase. It is the most severe form of tyrosinemia. Signs and symptoms appear early in life and include failure to thrive, vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, and bleeding tendency. It may result in liver and kidney failure. This syndrome occurs when part of chromosome 11 is missing."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A rare, genetic disorder that is present at birth and has two or more of the following symptoms: Wilms tumor (a type of kidney cancer); little or no iris (the colored part of the eye); defects in the sexual organs and urinary tract (the organs that make urine and pass it from the body); and below average mental ability. This syndrome occurs when part of chromosome 11 is missing.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3718"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C3718" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C3718</a></span></td></tr>

It is characterized by the appearance of accelerated aging following puberty. <tr data-subsets="base pre"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="X-linked Lymphoproliferative Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="X-linked Lymphoproliferative Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C61246" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>X-linked Lymphoproliferative Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An X-linked immunodeficiency syndrome that exclusively affects males, although females can be carriers. <tr data-subsets="base lt"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="ALRN 6924"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="ALRN 6924" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C118669" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>ALRN 6924</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An orally available peptide inhibitor of both murine double minute 2 (MDM2) and murine double minute X (MDMX), with potential antineoplastic activity. Upon oral administration, sulanemadlin binds to both MDM2 and MDMX and interferes with their interaction with the transcriptional activation domain of the tumor suppressor protein p53. By preventing MDM2-p53 and MDMX-p53 interactions, p53 activity is restored, which leads to p53-mediated induction of tumor cell apoptosis. MDM2 and MDMX, negative regulators of p53 function, are often overexpressed in cancer cells."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An orally available peptide inhibitor of both murine double minute 2 (MDM2) and murine double minute X (MDMX), with potential antineoplastic activity. Upon oral administration, sulanemadlin binds to both MDM2 and MDMX and interferes with their interaction with the transcriptional activation domain of the tumor suppressor protein p53. By preventing MDM2-p53 and MDMX-p53 interactions, p53 activity is restored, which leads to p53-mediated induction of tumor cell apoptosis. MDM2 and MDMX, negative regulators of p53 function, are often overexpressed in cancer cells.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C118669"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C118669" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C118669</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Abemaciclib"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Abemaciclib" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C97660" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Abemaciclib</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An orally available cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor that targets the CDK4 (cyclin D1) and CDK6 (cyclin D3) cell cycle pathway, with potential antineoplastic activity. Abemaciclib specifically inhibits CDK4 and 6, thereby inhibiting retinoblastoma (Rb) protein phosphorylation in early G1. Inhibition of Rb phosphorylation prevents CDK-mediated G1-S phase transition, thereby arresting the cell cycle in the G1 phase, suppressing DNA synthesis and inhibiting cancer cell growth. Overexpression of the serine/threonine kinases CDK4/6, as seen in certain types of cancer, causes cell cycle deregulation."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An orally available cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor that targets the CDK4 (cyclin D1) and CDK6 (cyclin D3) cell cycle pathway, with potential antineoplastic activity. Abemaciclib specifically inhibits CDK4 and 6, thereby inhibiting retinoblastoma (Rb) protein phosphorylation in early G1. Inhibition of Rb phosphorylation prevents CDK-mediated G1-S phase transition, thereby arresting the cell cycle in the G1 phase, suppressing DNA synthesis and inhibiting cancer cell growth. Overexpression of the serine/threonine kinases CDK4/6, as seen in certain types of cancer, causes cell cycle deregulation.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C97660"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C97660" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C97660</a></span></td></tr>

It is also used to reverse the toxicity of high doses of acetaminophen.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C200"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C200" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C200</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Adalimumab"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Adalimumab" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C65216" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Adalimumab</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A recombinant, human IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), with immunomodulating activity. TNF-alpha, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, is upregulated in various autoimmune diseases."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A recombinant, human IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), with immunomodulating activity. Upon administration, adalimumab binds to TNF-alpha, thereby preventing its binding to the p55 and p75 TNF cell surface receptors and inhibiting TNF-mediated immune responses. TNF-alpha, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, is upregulated in various autoimmune diseases.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C65216"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C65216" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C65216</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Akt Inhibitor MK2206"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Akt Inhibitor MK2206" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C90581" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Akt Inhibitor MK2206</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An orally bioavailable allosteric inhibitor of the serine/threonine protein kinase Akt (protein kinase B) with potential antineoplastic activity. Akt inhibitor MK2206 binds to and inhibits the activity of Akt in a non-ATP competitive manner, which may result in the inhibition of the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and tumor cell proliferation and the induction of tumor cell apoptosis. Activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway is frequently associated with tumorigenesis and dysregulated PI3K/Akt signaling may contribute to tumor resistance to a variety of antineoplastic agents"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An orally bioavailable allosteric inhibitor of the serine/threonine protein kinase Akt (protein kinase B) with potential antineoplastic activity. Akt inhibitor MK2206 binds to and inhibits the activity of Akt in a non-ATP competitive manner, which may result in the inhibition of the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and tumor cell proliferation and the induction of tumor cell apoptosis. <tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Alpelisib"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Alpelisib" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C94214" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Alpelisib</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An orally bioavailable phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor with potential antineoplastic activity. Alpelisib specifically inhibits PI3K in the PI3K/AKT kinase (or protein kinase B) signaling pathway, thereby inhibiting the activation of the PI3K signaling pathway. This may result in inhibition of tumor cell growth and survival in susceptible tumor cell populations. Activation of the PI3K signaling pathway is frequently associated with tumorigenesis. Dysregulated PI3K signaling may contribute to tumor resistance to a variety of antineoplastic agents."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An orally bioavailable phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor with potential antineoplastic activity. Alpelisib specifically inhibits PI3K in the PI3K/AKT kinase (or protein kinase B) signaling pathway, thereby inhibiting the activation of the PI3K signaling pathway. This may result in inhibition of tumor cell growth and survival in susceptible tumor cell populations. Activation of the PI3K signaling pathway is frequently associated with tumorigenesis. Dysregulated PI3K signaling may contribute to tumor resistance to a variety of antineoplastic agents.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C94214"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C94214" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C94214</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct npc"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Amifostine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Amifostine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C488" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Amifostine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="The trihydrate form of a phosphorylated aminosulfhydryl compound. After dephosphorylation of amifostine by alkaline phosphatase to an active free sulfhydryl (thiol) metabolite, the thiol metabolite binds to and detoxifies cytotoxic platinum-containing metabolites of cisplatin and scavenges free radicals induced by cisplatin and ionizing radiation. The elevated activity of this agent in normal tissues results from both the relative abundance of alkaline phosphatase in normal tissues and the greater vascularity of normal tissues compared to tumor tissues."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The trihydrate form of a phosphorylated aminosulfhydryl compound. After dephosphorylation of amifostine by alkaline phosphatase to an active free sulfhydryl (thiol) metabolite, the thiol metabolite binds to and detoxifies cytotoxic platinum-containing metabolites of cisplatin and scavenges free radicals induced by cisplatin and ionizing radiation. The elevated activity of this agent in normal tissues results from both the relative abundance of alkaline phosphatase in normal tissues and the greater vascularity of normal tissues compared to tumor tissues.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C488"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C488" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C488</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Amsacrine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Amsacrine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C240" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Amsacrine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="An aminoacridine derivative with potential antineoplastic activity. Although its mechanism of action is incompletely defined, amsacrine may intercalate into DNA and inhibit topoisomerase II, resulting in DNA double-strand breaks, arrest of the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle, and cell death. This agent's cytotoxicity is maximal during the S phase of the cell cycle when topoisomerase levels are greatest. In addition, amsacrine may induce transcription of tumor promoter p53 protein and block p53 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, resulting in p53-dependent tumor cell apoptosis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An aminoacridine derivative with potential antineoplastic activity. Although its mechanism of action is incompletely defined, amsacrine may intercalate into DNA and inhibit topoisomerase II, resulting in DNA double-strand breaks, arrest of the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle, and cell death. This agent's cytotoxicity is maximal during the S phase of the cell cycle when topoisomerase levels are greatest. In addition, amsacrine may induce transcription of tumor promoter p53 protein and block p53 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, resulting in p53-dependent tumor cell apoptosis.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C240"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C240" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C240</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Anakinra"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Anakinra" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C38717" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Anakinra</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A recombinant human nonglycosylated interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist with potential antineoplastic activity. Blockade of IL-1 activity may inhibit the cascade of downstream pro-angiogenic factors such as vascular endothelial cell growth factor, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and IL-6, resulting in inhibition of tumor angiogenesis. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A recombinant human nonglycosylated interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist with potential antineoplastic activity. Anakinra binds to the IL-1 receptor, thereby blocking the binding of the IL-1 to and activation of its receptor. Blockade of IL-1 activity may inhibit the cascade of downstream pro-angiogenic factors such as vascular endothelial cell growth factor, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and IL-6, resulting in inhibition of tumor angiogenesis. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C38717"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C38717" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C38717</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Anastrozole"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Anastrozole" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1607" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Anastrozole</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A nonsteroidal inhibitor of estrogen synthesis that resembles paclitaxel in chemical structure.  As a third-generation aromatase inhibitor, anastrozole selectively binds to and reversibly inhibits aromatase, a cytochrome P-450 enzyme complex found in many tissues including those of the premenopausal ovary, liver, and breast; aromatase catalyzes the aromatization of androstenedione and testosterone into estrone and estradiol, the final step in estrogen biosynthesis.  In estrogen-dependent breast cancers, ananstrozole may inhibit tumor growth. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A nonsteroidal inhibitor of estrogen synthesis that resembles paclitaxel in chemical structure.  As a third-generation aromatase inhibitor, anastrozole selectively binds to and reversibly inhibits aromatase, a cytochrome P-450 enzyme complex found in many tissues including those of the premenopausal ovary, liver, and breast; aromatase catalyzes the aromatization of androstenedione and testosterone into estrone and estradiol, the final step in estrogen biosynthesis.  In estrogen-dependent breast cancers, ananstrozole may inhibit tumor growth. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1607"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C1607" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C1607</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base fa"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Anti-thymocyte Globulin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Anti-thymocyte Globulin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C278" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Anti-thymocyte Globulin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="Purified gamma globulin, with immunosuppressive activity. Obtained from animals that have been immunized with human thymocytes, antithymocyte globulin (ATG) specifically recognizes and destroys T lymphocytes. Although not completely understood, the mechanism of action appears to involve T lymphocyte clearance from the circulation and modulation of T lymphocyte activity. Administering ATG with chemotherapy prior to stem cell transplantation may reduce the risk of graft-versus-host (GVH) disease."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Purified gamma globulin, with immunosuppressive activity. Obtained from animals that have been immunized with human thymocytes, antithymocyte globulin (ATG) specifically recognizes and destroys T lymphocytes. Although not completely understood, the mechanism of action appears to involve T lymphocyte clearance from the circulation and modulation of T lymphocyte activity. Administering ATG with chemotherapy prior to stem cell transplantation may reduce the risk of graft-versus-host (GVH) disease.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C278"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C278" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C278</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Antineoplaston A10"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Antineoplaston A10" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1004" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Antineoplaston A10</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A piperidinedione antineoplaston with potential antineoplastic activity.  Antineoplaston A10 was originally isolated from human urine but is now synthetically derived.  This agent intercalates into DNA, resulting in cell cycle arrest in G1 phase, reduction of mitosis, and decreased protein synthesis.  Antineoplaston A10 may also inhibit ras-oncogene expression and activate tumor suppressor gene p53, leading to cell differentiation and apoptosis. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A piperidinedione antineoplaston with potential antineoplastic activity.  Antineoplaston A10 was originally isolated from human urine but is now synthetically derived.  This agent intercalates into DNA, resulting in cell cycle arrest in G1 phase, reduction of mitosis, and decreased protein synthesis.  Antineoplaston A10 may also inhibit ras-oncogene expression and activate tumor suppressor gene p53, leading to cell differentiation and apoptosis. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1004"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C1004" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C1004</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Antineoplaston AS2-1"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Antineoplaston AS2-1" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1613" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Antineoplaston AS2-1</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A 4:1 mixture of phenylacetate and phenylacetylgluatmine, degradation products of the antineoplaston agent A10.  Antineoplaston AS2-1 inhibits the incorporation of L-glutamine into tumor-cell proteins, leading to cell cycle arrest in the G1 phase and inhibition of mitosis.  This agent may also inhibit RAS oncogene expression and activate tumor suppressor gene p53, resulting in cell differentiation and apoptosis. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A 4:1 mixture of phenylacetate and phenylacetylgluatmine, degradation products of the antineoplaston agent A10.  Antineoplaston AS2-1 inhibits the incorporation of L-glutamine into tumor-cell proteins, leading to cell cycle arrest in the G1 phase and inhibition of mitosis.  This agent may also inhibit RAS oncogene expression and activate tumor suppressor gene p53, resulting in cell differentiation and apoptosis. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1613"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C1613" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C1613</a></span></td></tr>

Aspirin belongs to the family of drugs called nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents. <tr data-subsets="base fprh"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Aspacytarabine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Aspacytarabine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1614" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Aspacytarabine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A semisynthetic derivative of the nucleoside-like antineoplastic antibiotic spicamycin, originally isolated from the bacterium Streptomyces alanosinicus.  KRN 5500 inhibits protein synthesis by interfering with endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus functions.  This agent also induces cell differentiation and caspase-dependent apoptosis. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A semisynthetic derivative of the nucleoside-like antineoplastic antibiotic spicamycin, originally isolated from the bacterium Streptomyces alanosinicus.  KRN 5500 inhibits protein synthesis by interfering with endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus functions.  This agent also induces cell differentiation and caspase-dependent apoptosis. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1614"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C1614" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C1614</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base lt"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Atezolizumab"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Atezolizumab" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C106250" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Atezolizumab</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A humanized, Fc optimized, monoclonal antibody directed against the protein ligand PD-L1 (programmed cell death-1 ligand 1; CD274), with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Atezolizumab binds to PD-L1, blocking its binding to and activation of its receptor programmed death 1 (PD-1; PDCD1) expressed on activated T-cells, which may enhance the T-cell-mediated immune response to neoplasms and reverse T-cell inactivation. In addition, by binding to PD-L1, atezolizumab also prevents binding of this ligand to B7.1 (CD80) expressed on activated T cells, which further enhances the T-cell-mediated immune response. PD-L1 is overexpressed on many human cancer cell types and on various tumor-infiltrating immune cells. PD-L1 binding to PD-1 on T-cells suppresses the immune system and results in increased immune evasion. PD-1, a transmembrane protein, is a negative regulator of the immune system that limits the expansion and survival of CD8+ T cells. The Fc region of atezolizumab is modified in such a way that it does not induce either antibody-dependent cytotoxicity (ADCC) or complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A humanized, Fc optimized, monoclonal antibody directed against the protein ligand PD-L1 (programmed cell death-1 ligand 1; CD274), with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Atezolizumab binds to PD-L1, blocking its binding to and activation of its receptor programmed death 1 (PD-1; PDCD1) expressed on activated T-cells, which may enhance the T-cell-mediated immune response to neoplasms and reverse T-cell inactivation. In addition, by binding to PD-L1, atezolizumab also prevents binding of this ligand to B7.1 (CD80) expressed on activated T cells, which further enhances the T-cell-mediated immune response. PD-L1 is overexpressed on many human cancer cell types and on various tumor-infiltrating immune cells. PD-L1 binding to PD-1 on T-cells suppresses the immune system and results in increased immune evasion. PD-1, a transmembrane protein, is a negative regulator of the immune system that limits the expansion and survival of CD8+ T cells. The Fc region of atezolizumab is modified in such a way that it does not induce either antibody-dependent cytotoxicity (ADCC) or complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC).</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C106250"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C106250" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C106250</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Atorvastatin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Atorvastatin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C61527" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Atorvastatin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A synthetic lipid-lowering agent. Atorvastatin competitively inhibits hepatic hydroxymethyl-glutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, the enzyme which catalyzes the conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a key step in cholesterol synthesis. Atorvastatin also increases the number of LDL receptors on hepatic cell surfaces to enhance uptake and catabolism of LDL and reduces LDL production and the number of LDL particles. This agent lowers plasma cholesterol and lipoprotein levels and modulates immune responses by suppressing MHC II (major histocompatibility complex II) on interferon gamma-stimulated, antigen-presenting cells such as human vascular endothelial cells. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A synthetic lipid-lowering agent. Atorvastatin competitively inhibits hepatic hydroxymethyl-glutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, the enzyme which catalyzes the conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a key step in cholesterol synthesis. Atorvastatin also increases the number of LDL receptors on hepatic cell surfaces to enhance uptake and catabolism of LDL and reduces LDL production and the number of LDL particles. This agent lowers plasma cholesterol and lipoprotein levels and modulates immune responses by suppressing MHC II (major histocompatibility complex II) on interferon gamma-stimulated, antigen-presenting cells such as human vascular endothelial cells. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C61527"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C61527" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C61527</a></span></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base fa_v1.0-draft ls lt"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Azathioprine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Azathioprine" data-pv-meaning="rxcui:1256" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Azathioprine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="azathioprine"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>azathioprine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="rxcui:1256"><span><a href="https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">rxcui:1256</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="BXQ-350 Nanovesicle Formulation"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="BXQ-350 Nanovesicle Formulation" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C131491" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>BXQ-350 Nanovesicle Formulation</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A stable, nanovesicle formulation composed of a synthetic form of the human glycoprotein saposin C (SapC) linked to the phospholipid dioleoylphosphatidylserine (DOPS), with potential antineoplastic activity. Upon intravenous administration, the BXQ-350 nanovesicle formulation selectively targets and preferentially accumulates in tumor vessels and cells, due to the leaky nature of tumor vasculature and the presence of phosphatidylserine (PS) lipids in tumor cell membranes. Upon binding to the phospholipids in the tumor cell membrane, SapC fuses with the membrane and is internalized leading to its accumulation within the internal membrane. SapC becomes active in the acidic tumor microenvironment and as a lysosomal sphingolipid activator protein, activates lysosomal enzymes, such as beta-glucosidase, acid sphingomyelinase, and beta-galactosylceramidase. This leads to the degradation of glucosylceramide and sphingomyelin, and the conversion of galactosylceramide to ceramide, respectively. This elevates intracellular ceramide levels, activates caspases and induces ceramide-mediated apoptosis, which together lead to an inhibition of tumor cell growth. SapC plays key roles in lipid transport and organization of biological membranes and has strong lipid membrane binding activity."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A stable, nanovesicle formulation composed of a synthetic form of the human glycoprotein saposin C (SapC) linked to the phospholipid dioleoylphosphatidylserine (DOPS), with potential antineoplastic activity. Upon intravenous administration, the BXQ-350 nanovesicle formulation selectively targets and preferentially accumulates in tumor vessels and cells, due to the leaky nature of tumor vasculature and the presence of phosphatidylserine (PS) lipids in tumor cell membranes. Upon binding to the phospholipids in the tumor cell membrane, SapC fuses with the membrane and is internalized leading to its accumulation within the internal membrane. SapC becomes active in the acidic tumor microenvironment and as a lysosomal sphingolipid activator protein, activates lysosomal enzymes, such as beta-glucosidase, acid sphingomyelinase, and beta-galactosylceramidase. This leads to the degradation of glucosylceramide and sphingomyelin, and the conversion of galactosylceramide to ceramide, respectively. This elevates intracellular ceramide levels, activates caspases and induces ceramide-mediated apoptosis, which together lead to an inhibition of tumor cell growth. SapC plays key roles in lipid transport and organization of biological membranes and has strong lipid membrane binding activity.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C131491"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C131491" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C131491</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base cns"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Belinostat"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Belinostat" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C48812" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Belinostat</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A novel hydroxamic acid-type histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor with antineoplastic activity. Belinostat targets HDAC enzymes, thereby inhibiting tumor cell proliferation, inducing apoptosis, promoting cellular differentiation, and inhibiting angiogenesis. This agent may sensitize drug-resistant tumor cells to other antineoplastic agents, possibly through a mechanism involving the down-regulation of thymidylate synthase."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A novel hydroxamic acid-type histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor with antineoplastic activity. Belinostat targets HDAC enzymes, thereby inhibiting tumor cell proliferation, inducing apoptosis, promoting cellular differentiation, and inhibiting angiogenesis. This agent may sensitize drug-resistant tumor cells to other antineoplastic agents, possibly through a mechanism involving the down-regulation of thymidylate synthase.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C48812"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C48812" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C48812</a></span></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bendamustine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bendamustine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C73261" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bendamustine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-description" title="A bifunctional mechlorethamine derivative with alkylating and antimetabolite activities. Although the exact mechanism of action of bendamustine is unknown, this agent appears to alkylate and crosslink macromolecules, resulting in DNA, RNA and protein synthesis inhibition, and eventually the induction of apoptosis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A bifunctional mechlorethamine derivative with alkylating and antimetabolite activities. Although the exact mechanism of action of bendamustine is unknown, this agent appears to alkylate and crosslink macromolecules, resulting in DNA, RNA and protein synthesis inhibition, and eventually the induction of apoptosis.</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C73261"><span><a href="https://evsexplore.semantics.cancer.gov/evsexplore/concept/ncit/C73261" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ncit:C73261</a></span></td></tr>
